args.summary:
This webpage from Flexiv (非夕) discusses how adaptive robots can serve as flexible "seasoned craftsmen" for polishing and grinding applications. It first outlines why grinding/polishing scenarios are difficult to automate: high requirements for force control capability, low solution universality (long testing/debugging cycles), and lack of reliable hardware that can withstand wear on robot bodies and peripheral equipment. Grinding needs are diverse, categorized by workpiece type and abrasive tool type.

The article then explains the core underlying capabilities needed for high-quality grinding/polishing:
1. **Surface tracking and trajectory learning** - Since 2019, Flexiv has tested surface-tracking algorithms for contact scenarios, enabling robots to automatically follow complex random surfaces, record trajectories and pressure states, and self-learn control strategies for grinding tasks.
2. **Surface conformance** - Using whole-body force control, adaptive robots achieve real-time surface conformance, especially for complex large-curvature surfaces, similar to how a human hand conforms.
3. **Force-position hybrid control dynamic performance** - Capable of high-speed grinding with stable maximum linear velocity up to 800mm/s (even 1000mm/s in some applications), with Rizon拂晓 series force control accuracy reaching 0.6N even in high-speed dynamic motion.
4. **Anti-interference capability + spatial flexibility** - Reliable interference resistance ensures higher grinding quality, and the seven-joint DOF design (vs. six-DOF limitations) avoids singular configurations, enabling continuous zero-defect constant/variable force control in large workspaces.

Chief Robot Scientist 钟书耘 (Zhong Shuyun) highlights four core advantages:
1. **Broader application range** - Robot stiffness can be flexibly adjusted to handle contrasting needs, from high-stiffness automotive weld-spot grinding (high vibration) to flexible conformant control for silicone earphone mold-line grinding at 0.5N force control.
2. **Better process quality** - Self-learning capability automatically adjusts control strategies based on environmental feedback. In phone frame grinding, dynamic force control accuracy reaches 1N with force fluctuations of 2-3N during cut-in/out, avoiding over-polishing. Insulator grinding achieves 1-2N dynamic force control accuracy.
3. **Efficient debugging and deployment** - Error tolerance from millimeters to centimeters automatically compensates; the graphical programming system Flexiv Elements enables rapid trajectory setup. In aluminum casting grinding, new process validation was completed in only two days; laser weld grinding deployment was achieved within one day.
4. **Higher overall cost-effectiveness** - Generally saves approximately 50% of costs compared to traditional automation, because the highly integrated force-controlled robot eliminates external sensors and floating grinding heads. Solutions can adapt to multiple grinding tools, can mount dual grinding heads simultaneously for different process steps, and support external TCP grinding solutions for kitchenware and automotive parts.

The article concludes that grinding/polishing remains a long-term focus area for Flexiv, and its advanced force control capabilities extend to other surface treatment tasks, positioning adaptive robots as flexible, universal, professional "robot craftsmen" for industry automation.

压紧力和砂带速度可以在 ABG 上独立控制。变力控制和皮带速度的结合优化了所有材料的表面处理并节省了工作步骤。即使在更换砂带时，也无需重新调整。作为灵敏主动型磨床，ABG是用于最高水平的打磨、抛光和去毛刺的定制解决方案。

![](https://www.ferrobotics.com/app/uploads/2020/11/thn-yt-FER-ACF-12.jpg)

##### 裸露混凝土的打磨

现代建筑的特点是创造力和独创性。ACF为混凝土的基本材料增添了活力的优雅。由于表面公差的交互式补偿和一致的接触力，保证了最高的表面质量。

![](https://www.ferrobotics.com/app/uploads/2020/11/thn-yt-FER-AOK905-6.jpg)

##### 碳部件的接触敏感加工

灵敏的主动柔顺力控技术遵循表面轮廓，并独立调整与过程相关的公差。它产生进一步加工所需的表面光洁度，并达到最高质量的水平。因此，碳制成的产品可以轻松、可靠和自动地加工。

![](https://www.ferrobotics.com/app/uploads/2020/11/thn-yt-FER-AOK-16.jpg)

##### 涂漆复合材料零件的预打磨

ACF精密的复合材料零件在每周7天，每天24小时的操作中获得完美的自动抛光。由于力控制，ACF保证了均匀的表面粗糙度，从而显着提高了油漆质量并消除了可能的成型缺陷。

![](https://www.ferrobotics.com/app/uploads/2020/11/thn-yt-FER-ACF-13.jpg)

##### 手动辅助打磨

ACF与人类合作，为世界市场提供了最高质量标准，磨料消耗量显著降低。由于其可靠的计量力和对表面的完美适应性，ACF保证了可重复的质量，并显着降低了磨料消耗。

![](https://www.ferrobotics.com/app/uploads/2020/11/thn-yt-FER-ABG-4.jpg)

##### 用于重型应用的砂带打磨解决方案

通过这个完整的解决方案，生产率提高了80%，同时磨料消耗减少了75%。专门开发的重磨解决方案可实现每小时高达 14 kg 物料的去除性能。优化的设计确保焊缝不会被磨穿。

![](https://www.ferrobotics.com/app/uploads/2020/11/thn-yt-FER-ACF-15.jpg)

##### 铸件的全自动加工

这种全自动处理确保了顺利安装所需的恒定质量。对于链条驱动车辆的轴承座，必须去除浇口和毛刺。在此过程的初始步骤中，浇口的位置由激光选择。在第二步中，浇口自动完全移除，从而取代繁重的体力劳动。

![](https://www.ferrobotics.com/app/uploads/2020/11/thn-yt-FER-ACF-18.jpg)

##### 全自动公差补偿

ACF是一种主动平衡元件，可自动补偿公差，从而计量并精确地保持所需的力水平。作为一种主动灵敏的自动化解决方案，ACF 即使在基于材料的差异的情况下也能确保稳定的质量。即使是 0.2 mm 的单板也不会欠缺打磨。

![](https://www.ferrobotics.com/app/uploads/2020/11/thn-yt-FER-ACF-20.jpg)

##### 食品加工行业的自动化表面处理

菲洛博迪在全自动机器人工艺中实现了4μm的最大表面粗糙度。只有通过ACF和匹配的打磨工具实现自动化，才能保证这一决定性工作步骤的精确力控制和稳定性。这种表面光洁度对产品质量至关重要。

![](https://www.ferrobotics.com/app/uploads/2020/12/thn-yt-FER-ACF-K-14.jpg)

##### 使用 ACF-Kit自动去毛刺 - 角磨机

用户友好的即插即用工具ACF-Kit专为满足灵活生产的需求而开发。由于采用模块化设计，工具可以在几秒钟内更换，从而在很短的时间内用于各种应用。该套件包含大量可连接设备，适用于各种表面加工，是打磨几乎所有形状和材料的理想选择。

![](https://www.ferrobotics.com/app/uploads/2020/12/thn-yt-FER-ACF-K-15.jpg)

##### 测试自动铬镍打磨

多功能ACF-Kit可实现各种形状和材料的自动化表面处理，几乎无需实施工作。由于其在整个表面过程中的主动力控制和恒定的接触力，ACF-Kit保证了最佳的打磨质量，就像在这个铬镍表面上一样。

![](https://www.ferrobotics.com/app/uploads/2020/11/thn-yt-FER-AAK-1.jpg)

##### 使用 AAK 自动找平焊缝

由于可靠计量的接触力和对表面的完美适应，AAK可提供始终如一的高表面质量，这是手动无法实现的。使用AAK焊接接缝自动研磨，不需要任何返工。

This is the FerRobotics company product page (in Chinese) for robotic surface finishing solutions, covering grinding, sanding, polishing, and deburring across various materials and industries. FerRobotics positions itself as a technology leader in automated surface finishing, with products that "feel" what they do, providing active force control (active compliant force control / ACF technology) for consistent quality even in 24/7 operations.

KEY PRODUCT LINES:
- ASK (Active Sensitive Kit): flexible force-controlled grinding head for automated grinding of roof seams, door frame grinding, and weld seam cleaning in automotive body shell work
- AOK (Active Orbital Kit): orbital sander kit with variants including AOK XS, AOK601 (three-head orbital sander), AOK905 for various sanding/polishing applications
- ACF (Active Compliant Flange): active compensation element for robot-compliant automation in grinding, polishing, deburring applications
- ACF-Kit: modular, user-friendly plug-and-play tool set developed for collaborative robots (cobots) with wide tool selection
- AAK (Active Angle Kit): heavy-duty angle grinder solutions including AAK HD for heavy material removal
- ABG (Active Belt Grinder): flexible belt sander for medium and small workpieces (e.g., stainless steel, fan blades, exhaust pipes)

APPLICATIONS COVERED BY INDUSTRY:
1. Automotive: roof seam grinding, paint defect repair on topcoat, spot repair automation, weld seam leveling, exhaust pipe grinding, car door grinding, anti-flash welding, thin-wall workpiece grinding (3-8N force control), motorcycle part polishing, car fender polishing, deburring of injection-molded parts
2. General industry: guitar body sanding, fireplace grinding (HASE Kaminofenbau with SHL AG partner), propeller grinding, bathtub sanding, wood part sanding, acrylic glass polishing, furniture sanding, glass engraving, food industry stainless steel surface finishing (max 4μm surface roughness), cast part processing, concrete grinding, carbon component processing, large surface grinding (AOK601 for railway vehicles, buses, aircraft, ship hulls)
3. Aerospace: aircraft wing grinding (AOK601), turbine blade/impeller grinding (with accell and Toyota; with AV&R for compressor blades), surface finishing for minimal air turbulence

KEY STATISTICS AND SELLING POINTS:
- 24/7 operation capability with consistent quality
- Reduced cycle times, lower costs, higher productivity
- Replaces 3D jobs (dirty, difficult, dangerous work)
- Active force control with automatic tolerance compensation
- Constant contact force reduces abrasive consumption
- Integrated suction reduces cleaning work
- ACF achieves sustained low force of 3-8N for thin-wall applications
- Complete heavy-duty grinding solution achieves 80% productivity increase with 75% less abrasive consumption, material removal up to 14 kg/hour
- Rapid ROI: fireplace grinding solution achieved ROI in under 2 years
- ABG enables automated polishing certified for medical device industry (hip and knee implants)

The page also includes a consultation section inviting visitors to contact FerRobotics as the "global leader in flexible robotics market" with a "Perfect Feeling" brand tagline. Navigation categories include products, know-how, references, company, news, and contact sections, covering industries (automotive, general industry, aerospace) and applications (grinding/polishing/deburring, joining/gluing/assembly, handling, quality control, cobot applications).

## Mirka® 机器人打磨机和抛光机

![]() 

探索磨卡机器人打磨机和抛光机系列。磨卡 AIROS 是首款适用于工业机器人和协作机器人的智能电动机器人打磨机。这款自动化工业随机轨道式打磨机易于集成，可适应所有机械联轴器，为各个制造业提供高质量的打磨和抛光效果。磨卡 AIOS 是一款带有非随机轨道的机器人磨机，可用于自动点修。磨卡 AIROP 是一款随机轨道式机器人抛光机，配有先进的电动抛光头，与磨卡抛光垫和抛光液兼容。

## 使用精确转速管理

![]() 

自动打磨不仅更高效，而且更智能。磨卡的机器人打磨和抛光系统具有内置智能功能，可在打磨头和控制系统之间实现双向通信。这种功能可提供详细的状态更新并允许进行调整，让您完全控制打磨过程。此外，智能电动打磨解决方案还提供精确的转速控制，可进行配置，以满足每个加工阶段的具体要求。即使在负载增加的情况下，稳定的转速也能确保可靠的高质量打磨效果。

通用机器人的多功能解决方案

## 磨卡机器人打磨头：

磨卡机器人打磨头与市场上的大多数机器人手臂兼容。它们专为连续机器人打磨而设计，由于其紧凑轻巧的设计，适用于低负载机器人手臂。每个磨卡机器人打磨机都配有标准化 ISO 9409-1-80-6-M8 法兰，可使用适配器进行定制。使用快速电缆和真空软管连接器，安装非常简单。此外，磨卡机器人打磨头可以通过特殊的 UR 安装套件进行改装，以用于通用机器人协作解决方案。

表面打磨和精加工（如砂光、打磨、抛光和其他精加工过程）是耗时且劳动密集型的工艺，需要具有耐力和技能的操作工手动进行。

**一、协作喷涂机器人及其核心价值**

在开始选择厂家前，我们首先需要明确一个关键概念：**什么是协作喷涂机器人？** 简单来说，它是在传统工业喷涂机器人基础上，融入**协作机器人（Cobot）特性**的产物。它不仅具备精准、高效的自动化喷涂能力，更强调**安全、易用、灵活**，能够与人共享工作空间，无需复杂的安全围栏。

**Q：为什么协作机器人会成为喷涂自动化的新趋势？与传统方案相比有何优势？**

**A：** 协作喷涂机器人的兴起，主要源于制造业对**柔性生产**的迫切需求。传统的大型喷涂自动化生产线适合大批量、标准化产品，但面临初始投资高、换产调试耗时长的挑战。而协作机器人提供了更具性价比和灵活性的解决方案，其核心优势可概括为以下三点：

**1.** **更高的生产柔性**：轻松适应小批量、多品种的生产模式，通过**拖拽示教、视觉引导或数字孪生**等技术，能极大缩短新产品上线的编程调试时间。

**2.** **更低的部署门槛**：通常更轻便，安装要求低，且**人机协作的安全特性**减少了对全套安全围栏的依赖，初始投资和场地改造成本更具优势。

**3.** **更智能的工艺传承**：可通过**VR示教、动作捕捉**等技术，直接记录并复现优秀喷涂工人的工艺手法，实现“老师傅”经验的数字化传承与标准化复制。

**二、六大协作喷涂机器人厂家深度分析**

选择厂家不能仅看品牌，而需结合具体应用场景。以下对六家在不同细分领域具备特色的厂商进行分析，供读者参考：

**1、节卡机器人（JAKA）**

在协作喷涂机器人领域，节卡机器人（JAKA） 凭借其深度融合的智能化技术与卓越的柔性协作能力，已成为解决多品种、小批量柔性化生产挑战的杰出代表。其解决方案并非简单替代人工，而是通过一系列核心技术，重新定义了智能喷涂的效率和品质标准。

**核心技术：精准复现与简易编程的融合。**节卡智能喷涂的核心效能，首先建立在高精度运动控制与轨迹规划之上。其机器人（如JAKA Zu系列机器人）重复定位精度最高可达±0.02mm，确保了复杂曲面喷涂的一致性。更重要的是，其拖拽示教功能让经验得以数字化：熟练工人的最佳喷涂路径可被精准记录与重现，极大降低了编程门槛和调试时间。

[*展开全文*](javascript:;)

**智能感知：视觉引导与自适应学习**。其次，机器视觉与AI自适应技术构成了系统的“智能感官”。通过3D视觉精准识别工件并自动修正轨迹，结合AI算法优化参数。例如在汽车售后喷涂领域，节卡的智能仿生喷涂机器人应用灵活适配多款车型，实现高度自动化的流水线作业，并能通过离线编程技术让普通员工轻松操作，在提升标准化程度的同时，将工人从有害环境中解放。

**柔性协作：应对多品种生产的敏捷性。**面对个性化定制的核心痛点，节卡的柔性协作与快速换产能力优势凸显。在如烧烤架这类产品规格繁多、换型频繁的生产线上，其协作机器人通过拖拽示教，能在3分钟内完成产品切换，轨迹录制后一键即可调用。这种极高的柔性，完美应对了多品类、小批量的市场挑战，并可复制到3C、精密制造等广泛领域。

**丰富实践：从工具到生产理念的升级。**从实践案例看，节卡方案的价值得到实证。在汽车售后喷涂场景，它解决了技师水平参差、健康风险高的问题；在食品日化生产线，它则攻克了换产效率的瓶颈。其机器人平均无故障运行时间可达数万小时，在提升产能和涂料利用率方面表现显著，从长期看形成了明确的综合成本优势。

节卡机器人代表了喷涂自动化向 “更智能、更柔性、更易用” 方向的演进，节卡机器人提供一种深度融合AI、视觉与协作技术，旨在“解放生产力”的智能化生产理念，为企业在质量、效率与灵活性兼顾的竞争中提供关键支撑。

**2、库卡（KUKA）**

作为德系代表，以柔性定制化喷涂见长。它凭借TrueMotion轨迹优化技术和开放的KUKA.AppTech应用软件包，提供了高度灵活的协作安全版本解决方案。库卡机器人特别适合定制家具、小型金属件等多品种、小批量的个性化喷涂任务。若您注重机器人本体的运动控制性能与软件开放性，并需要深度定制喷涂工艺，库卡能够很好地满足这些要求。

**3、发那科（FANUC）**

工业机器人“四大家族”背景，将数十年工业可靠性基因注入协作机器人。其技术优势在于超低振动控制和高轨迹平滑度，提供可选洁净室机型，并具备极高的重复定位精度。这些特点使其在3C电子消费品、医疗器械等行业中应用广泛。如果您需要在高标准无尘车间内进行喷涂，发那科的精密机型是可靠的选择。

**4、川崎（Kawasaki）**

大负载、大臂展重载喷涂方面专家。其机器人采用高刚性机械结构，腕部负载能力强，臂展选择范围广。它主要应对风电叶片、工程机械、铁路车辆、等工件的喷涂作业挑战。对于传统重工业领域中大工件喷涂自动化需求，川崎的高负载机器人提供了关键的技术解决方案。

作为国产化与自适应喷涂的技术代表，集成了自适应喷涂算法和国产核心部件，本地化服务网络完善。它基于3D扫描的自适应喷涂技术，在汽车主机厂及零部件、家电、通用工业等领域有广泛应用，特别适合有进口替代和成本优化需求的客户。如果您在寻求性能接近国际品牌，同时兼具显著性价比优势和快速服务响应的解决方案，埃夫特提供了一个平衡而务实的选择。

**6、长广溪智造**

“车规级高速协作机器人”倡议者。该厂商主要适用于对喷涂工艺一致性和漆面质量有要求的领域，例如汽车零部件钣喷、高端自行车架等工件的喷涂。

args.summary:
This is a comprehensive purchasing guide (dated December 28, 2025, published by JAKA节卡机器人 on Sohu) for collaborative spraying robots (协作喷涂机器人), covering the technology's core value, six manufacturer analyses, and key solution components.

**Core Concept & Value:**
Collaborative spraying robots combine traditional industrial spraying automation with cobot characteristics—offering precision and efficiency while prioritizing safety, ease of use, and flexibility that allows human-robot workspace sharing without complex safety fencing. Three core advantages over traditional systems: (1) Higher production flexibility for small-batch, multi-variety production via drag teaching, visual guidance, or digital twin technologies; (2) Lower deployment barriers with lighter equipment, reduced safety fencing needs, and lower initial investment; (3) Smarter process inheritance through VR teaching and motion capture to digitize experienced worker techniques.

**Six Manufacturer Analyses:**
1. **节卡机器人 (JAKA)** – Highlighted as the leading example; achieves ±0.02mm repeat positioning accuracy (JAKA Zu series), uses drag teaching for digitalizing expert spray paths, 3D vision for workpiece recognition and trajectory correction, AI adaptive algorithms, and can complete product switching in 3 minutes via drag teaching. Applied in automotive aftermarket spraying, food/daily chemical production lines, and BBQ grill manufacturing. Robots feature tens of thousands of hours of mean time between failures (MTBF).
2. **库卡 (KUKA)** – German representative known for flexible customized spraying, TrueMotion trajectory optimization, open KUKA.AppTech software; suited for custom furniture and small metal parts spraying.
3. **发那科 (FANUC)** – From the "Big Four" industrial robot families; ultra-low vibration control, high trajectory smoothness, optional cleanroom models, very high repeat positioning accuracy; suited for 3C electronics and medical devices in dust-free environments.
4. **川崎 (Kawasaki)** – Heavy-load, large-reach spraying expert with high-rigidity structures and strong wrist load capacity; handles wind turbine blades, construction machinery, and railway vehicle spraying.
5. **埃夫特 (EFORT)** – Chinese domestic technology representative with adaptive spraying algorithms and domestic core components, complete local service network, 3D scanning-based adaptive spraying; applied in automotive OEMs, parts, home appliances, and general industry; offers cost-effective import substitution.
6. **长广溪智造** – Promotes "automotive-grade high-speed collaborative robots"; suited for automotive parts sheet metal spraying and high-end bicycle frame spraying.

**Complete Solution Components:**
Beyond the robot body, a full solution requires a "body + process package + integration" trinity: (1) Process packages with dedicated spraying software integrating flow control, atomization parameters, and trajectory planning databases; (2) Peripheral systems including explosion-proof paint supply, quick color-change modules, and AI vision quality inspection; (3) Integration and service capabilities for turnkey delivery (design through installation, commissioning, and training) with ongoing technical support.

**Future Outlook:** Spraying robots will evolve toward smarter, more collaborative, and greener solutions, with AI further optimizing processes autonomously and deeper human-robot collaboration shifting repetitive, heavy, and hazardous work to robots while humans focus on creativity, supervision, and maintenance.

args.summary: This webpage, from Robotmaster (a Hypertherm product), covers robotic painting, spraying, and coating applications. The page highlights how Robotmaster enables precise control of spray angles, speed, and flow intensity across surfaces—critical for industries like automotive and aerospace. Key benefits of using Robotmaster for robotic paint/spray applications include: easy robot program generation directly from CAD models with minimal modifications for changes in spray shape, nozzle diameter, nozzle-to-part distance, and number of coats; automatic entry/exit extension beyond the CAD model; automated management of step intervals (eliminating the need for reprogramming); uniform step spacing for consistent coating; and automatic tool orientation management to minimize wrist rotation and extend robot reach. The software simulates coverage using spray parameters to automate optimized path programming, ensuring full surface coverage with minimal effort, reduced paint waste, and optimized cycle times. # 自主喷漆机器人行业前景再定义：十五五目标下的市场规模与增长引擎—2026版报告

![在这里插入图片描述](https://i-blog.csdnimg.cn/direct/28299dc10ac149e19ee8953657cd4601.png#pic_center)  
 自主喷漆机器人行业深度调研报告解读：2021-2032年全球市场全景洞察  
 精准的市场洞察是企业制定战略、规避风险、捕捉机遇的核心能力。环洋市场咨询（Global Info Research）最新发布的《全球自主喷漆机器人行业总体规模、主要厂商及IPO上市调研报告，2026-2032》，涵盖2021至2032年完整历史数据与未来趋势预测，为自主喷漆机器人行业参与者提供极具价值的决策参考。

核心观点：核心总结 2025年，全球自动喷涂机器人产量约为6,821台，平均价格约为42,000美元 欧洲约占2025年自主喷漆机器人市场供应商收入的39% 大型资产船舶及风电涂层系统约占2025年市场收入的31% 中国总部厂商约贡献2025年市场收入的27%并形成最广泛制造基础 移动式建筑喷涂系统约占2025年市场收入的26% 核心正式供应商池包含30家已验证制造商及系统提供商 行业发展趋势 自主喷漆机器人正在由预设轨迹自动化向感知驱动和工艺感知型自主化演进。早期设备主要重复执行人工示教轨迹，新一代产品则逐步融合三维扫描、机器视觉、表面建图和自动路径生成，以适应变化工件及非结构化作业环境。产品功能也正从单一喷涂延伸至表面预处理、涂层施加、质量监测和施工数据记录的协同闭环。大型资产设备更多采用磁吸附爬壁或绳索悬挂平台，建筑产品则将移动底盘、长臂机械结构和墙面自动识别结合起来；工业设备持续引入扫描生成轨迹及示教学习技术，以满足多品种、小批量生产需求。商业模式也由设备直接销售向租赁、按项目收费和机器人即服务扩展，降低客户一次性资本投入。目前商业化设备已经能够实现喷涂单元集成、半自主表面移动，以及面向工业资产和风电部件的机器人涂层施工。 市场动态 驱动因素 市场需求主要受到职业安全要求、熟练喷涂工短缺、人工成本上升及涂层质量一致性要求提高的共同推动。喷涂作业可能涉及有害物质、可燃雾滴、挥发性气体和受限空间风险，船体、储罐、风机及建筑外墙还叠加高空作业和进入成本。自主喷漆机器人能够将人员转移出直接喷涂区域，并保持更稳定的喷涂距离、运动速度和材料流量。政策支持也在拓宽可应用市场，中国“机器人+”应用行动将喷涂、建筑装饰、自主导航和智能感知列为机器人重点应用方向，有利于制造业、建筑及基础设施维护领域开展产品开发和示范应用。 限制因素 自主喷漆机器人的应用仍受到初始投资较高、项目工程化程度较深和设备利用率不确定等因素限制。适合平整墙面的设备通常难以直接用于曲面储罐、船体或复杂工业零部件，使制造商难以通过单一标准化平台分摊全部研发成本。除机器人本体外，客户往往还需要配置供漆设备、通风设施、防爆系统、现场改造、操作培训及既有流程集成。频繁换色、清洗维护、表面状态变化和不同涂料体系之间的兼容问题也可能降低设备可用率。对于项目量不足或施工计划不连续的中小承包商，直接购置设备的投资回收周期可能缺乏吸引力。 市场机遇 未来机会主要集中在大面积、高风险进入和涂层需求重复性较强的应用。储罐、船舶、海工结构、风电叶片、工业建筑及高层外墙通常需要脚手架、绳索作业或较长停机时间，自动化替代具有较清晰的经济价值。汽车修补也是具有潜力的方向，机器视觉和车型识别可支持车身面板或整车喷涂路径自动生成。柔性制造领域则可通过扫描生成轨迹和自学习技术减少小批量及频繁换型工件的编程投入。设备租赁和机器人即服务有望推动年作业量不足以支持直接采购的承包商采用设备，持续性的软件、维护及工艺数据服务也为供应商改善收入稳定性提供空间。 行业风险与挑战 行业长期挑战在于将技术演示转化为可重复、可盈利的规模化部署。实际作业环境中存在障碍物、风力、粉尘、光照变化、基材不平整及涂料黏度波动，均可能影响轨迹精度和涂层一致性。供应商不仅需要机器人研发能力，还必须具备涂装工艺、安全系统和现场服务经验，因此市场进入门槛高于普通自动化设备。覆盖率、传递效率、膜厚、缺陷率及人工干预次数等指标在不同应用之间尚缺乏统一评价体系。机器人在示教、维护、故障恢复及人员接近运动设备时也会产生新的安全要求，即使减少了人工直接喷涂，通风、防爆、紧急停止和机器人风险评估仍然不可缺少。 产业链分析 自主喷漆机器人上游主要包括工业机器人本体、移动底盘、磁吸附机构、电机、减速器、伺服驱动、控制器、机器视觉相机、三维扫描仪、激光雷达、力传感器、喷枪、泵体、软管、雾化设备及防爆电气部件。涂料与涂层材料供应商也会通过黏度、固化特性、雾化性能及自动清洗和换色兼容性影响系统表现。软件层主要涉及同步定位与建图、点云处理、目标识别、路径规划、数字孪生、工艺仿真和喷涂参数数据库。精密零部件及通过安全认证的硬件构成设备成本的重要部分，而专用感知、控制软件及应用工程能力则决定产品差异化程度。 中游企业负责将上述部件整合为自主移动机器人、爬壁机器人、悬挂机器人、空中平台及自适应工业喷涂工作站。行业价值创造重点并不只在机器人本体，而在表面感知、路径生成、喷涂工艺控制、机械可靠性及现场部署能力。供应商可通过设备销售、交钥匙系统、软件许可、维护合同、设备租赁、机器人即服务或涂层施工项目获得收入。下游客户包括建筑承包商、专业涂装服务商、船厂、船东、储罐运营商、风机制造商与运营商、汽车维修网络及工业制造企业。拥有可重复使用软件模块和工艺数据库的企业通常具备更好的利润扩展能力，而高度定制化项目虽然合同金额较高，也会产生更多工程设计、调试和售后成本。 细分市场分析 从平台架构看，自主移动机械臂适用范围最广，磁吸附爬壁机器人则主要集中于钢制储罐、船舶和塔筒。固定式、轨道式及龙门式扫描生成轨迹系统在工件能够进入受控喷涂区域的工厂环境中仍具优势，绳索悬挂和空中平台主要服务传统设备难以经济进入的表面。从编程方式看，三维扫描生成轨迹和视觉自动规划预计将随着客户缩短换型时间和提高柔性生产需求而扩大应用，示教学习则仍适合希望降低操作难度、但不计划大规模改变现有生产布局的工业客户。 下游市场机会 建筑、船舶维护、石油天然气储运、风电、汽车修补及柔性工业制造构成自主喷漆机器人的主要下游机会。建筑客户更加关注设备部署速度、操作简易性以及对门窗、转角和不规则现场条件的适应能力；船厂和储罐运营商更重视吸附可靠性、耐腐蚀性、防爆能力、涂层效率及减少脚手架需求；风电客户看重缩短停机时间，并希望在一次服务中整合检测、清洗、修复和涂层施工。汽车维修网络需要稳定的外观质量、喷漆房兼容性和快速车型识别，工业制造企业则更加关注编程时间、材料传递效率及与既有产线的集成。因此，围绕明确作业流程开发的专用解决方案，比试图以单一通用机器人覆盖全部喷涂场景更具商业化可行性。 地区分析 欧洲是2025年最大的供应区域，约占所定义市场收入的39%。该地区在自学习工业喷涂、储罐和船舶涂层、风电机器人服务及专业建筑机器人方面具备较强能力，并拥有成熟的涂装工程基础和工业资产安全维护需求。中国约占27%，拥有最广泛的已识别制造商群体，产品覆盖建筑、汽车修补、爬壁平台、风电部件及一般工业喷涂，但企业在产品成熟度、财务透明度及出口能力方面差异较大。北美约占20%，市场特征是更加重视机器人即服务和机器人施工承包模式。以色列已在建筑机器人领域形成专业化定位，印度和东南亚仍处于较早阶段，主要由建筑装修机器人初创企业推动。日本、韩国和台湾拥有较强的传统机器人及自动化产业基础，但按照本报告自主化口径形成独立对外销售产品的企业数量相对有限。 竞争格局 自主喷漆机器人市场呈现应用专业化驱动的分散竞争结构，尚未形成单一标准产品主导所有场景的格局。第一梯队主要由拥有真实设备、重复客户项目、自有感知或路径规划能力及现场交付资源的供应商构成，其中部分企业通过风电、建筑或大型资产机器人施工服务实现商业化，另一些企业则向制造客户销售自学习机器人和交钥匙涂装单元。第二梯队集中于汽车修补、船厂、储罐、建筑装修及大型工业工件等专业场景，即使企业整体规模有限，也可依靠应用经验、定制能力和本地服务形成竞争力。中国厂商通常在制造成本、定制速度和国内工程支持方面具备优势，欧洲企业在专用涂层工艺、成熟工业渠道和高价值资产应用方面相对领先，北美企业则积极发展按项目收费及机器人即服务等持续收入模式。未来企业差异化将更多取决于自主路径生成、涂层质量反馈、可复用工艺数据库、设备利用率、安全认证以及能否向客户证明清晰的投资回报。  
 重点企业：Aerones Inc.、PaintJet, Inc.、埃夫特智能机器人股份有限公司、Qlayers B.V.、Okibo Ltd.、浙江史河科技有限公司、Lesta s.r.l.、广东博智林机器人有限公司、Epistolio S.r.l.、武汉湾流科技股份有限公司、Ventherm A/S、Tebulo Robotics、Apellix, LLC、ConBotics GmbH、深圳领鹊科技有限公司、AMBPR SAS、清研同创机器人（天津）有限公司、Finish Robotics、Eternal Robotics、深圳市行知行机器人技术有限公司

一、报告摘要：核心发现速览  
 报告开篇直击核心。您将清晰看到全球自主喷漆机器人的总产值及截至2032年的增长预测，了解行业财富总量与增长潜力。总产量与总消费量体现实物需求规模，年复合增长率（CAGR）则衡量行业吸引力与发展阶段。全球主要生产地区、消费地区及领先生产商一览无余，助您快速建立对自主喷漆机器人市场“体量、速度、主要玩家”的认知。

二、全球供给与需求分析：总量趋势把握  
 供给侧方面，报告展示自主喷漆机器人历史产值与产量数据并构建至2032年的预测模型。北美、欧洲、中国、日本等主要地区的产量、产值及增速一清二楚，帮助您识别自主喷漆机器人生产重心与供应链风险点。同时，技术创新、消费升级、政策利好等驱动因素，以及原材料价格波动、贸易壁垒等阻碍因素被系统梳理，产品高端化、智能化、绿色可持续等未来方向亦明确指出。  
 需求侧方面，美国、中国、欧洲、日本、韩国、东南亚、印度等自主喷漆机器人主要消费地区的市场销量逐一呈现，核心市场与高增长潜力区域一目了然。

三、行业竞争格局分析：解码市场态势  
 报告量化全球自主喷漆机器人主要生产商的产量、产值、平均价格、市场份额等关键指标，通过CR4、CR8等集中度分析判断市场结构类型。自主喷漆机器人主要厂商的产品组合、业务布局、目标市场等战略要素被深入分析，进入壁垒与核心竞争因素（品牌、渠道、研发、成本等）亦被清晰总结。

四、关键国别市场对比：聚焦战略要地  
 报告选取美国和中国进行深度对比，两国在自主喷漆机器人产值、产量、销量上的规模差异及全球份额一目了然。美国与中国自主喷漆机器人市场的本土生产商及其市场表现被逐一识别，欧洲、日韩等其他重要市场的自主喷漆机器人主要生产商亦在扫描之列，呈现完整的自主喷漆机器人行业全球视角。

五、细分市场深度剖析：挖掘增长蓝海  
 按产品类型（自主移动机械臂、磁吸附爬壁机器人、空中喷涂机器人、其他）和应用领域（建筑及建筑服务、造船及海工、石油及天然气、其他），报告分别分析自主喷漆机器人各细分市场的产量、产值、价格走势及未来增速。通过交叉分析，您将精准识别最具增长潜力的细分赛道，实现资源的高效投放。

This webpage is a deep-dive research report summary titled "自主喷漆机器人行业前景再定义：十五五目标下的市场规模与增长引擎—2026版报告" (Redefining the Outlook of the Autonomous Spray Painting Robot Industry: Market Size and Growth Engines Under the 15th Five-Year Plan's Goals—2026 Edition Report). It was published by user dongd703 on the DAMO Developer Matrix platform (DAMO开发者矩阵) on August 19, 2026, with 199 views.

**Key Market Statistics (2025):**
- Global autonomous spray painting robot production was approximately 6,821 units, with an average price of approximately $42,000 USD
- Europe accounted for approximately 39% of supplier revenue in 2025
- Large assets (ships and wind power coating systems) accounted for approximately 31% of 2025 market revenue
- China-headquartered manufacturers contributed approximately 27% of 2025 market revenue and have the broadest manufacturing base
- Mobile building spray systems accounted for approximately 26% of 2025 market revenue
- The verified supplier pool includes 30 manufacturers and system providers

**Industry Trends:**
- Autonomous spray painting robots are evolving from preset trajectory automation to perception-driven and process-aware autonomy
- Early devices repeated manually taught trajectories; new-generation products integrate 3D scanning, machine vision, surface mapping, and automatic path generation
- Product functions expanding from single spraying to surface pretreatment, coating application, quality monitoring, and construction data recording
- Business models shifting from direct equipment sales to leasing, per-project charging, and Robot-as-a-Service (RaaS)
- Magnetic adsorption wall-climbing or rope-suspended platforms used for large assets; building products combine mobile chassis, long-arm mechanisms, and automatic wall recognition

**Market Drivers:**
- Occupational safety requirements, shortage of skilled spray painters, rising labor costs, and demand for consistent coating quality
- Policy support including China's "Robot+" application initiative (机器人+应用行动) listing spraying, building decoration, autonomous navigation, and intelligent perception as key robot application areas

**Market Constraints:**
- High initial investment, deep project engineering requirements, and uncertain equipment utilization rates
- Devices suited for flat walls struggle with curved tanks, ship hulls, or complex industrial parts
- Additional costs for paint supply equipment, ventilation, explosion-proof systems, site renovation, operator training, and existing process integration
- Frequent color changes, cleaning/maintenance, surface state variations, and paint system compatibility issues reduce equipment availability

**Market Opportunities:**
- Large-area, high-risk-access applications with repetitive coating needs: tanks, ships, offshore structures, wind turbine blades, industrial buildings, and high-rise exterior walls
- Automotive refinishing (with machine vision and vehicle recognition)
- Flexible manufacturing via scan-generated trajectories and self-learning technologies
- Equipment leasing and RaaS to help contractors unable to justify direct purchases

**Industry Risks:**
- Challenges in converting technical demonstrations to repeatable, profitable scaled deployments
- Real-world obstacles: wind, dust, lighting variation, uneven substrates, paint viscosity fluctuations
- High market entry barriers requiring both robot R&D and coating process expertise
- Lack of unified evaluation metrics for coverage, transfer efficiency, film thickness, defect rate, and manual intervention frequency

**Industry Chain Analysis:**
- Upstream: industrial robot bodies, mobile chassis, magnetic adsorption mechanisms, motors, reducers, servo drives, controllers, vision cameras, 3D scanners, LiDAR, force sensors, spray guns, pumps, hoses, atomization equipment, explosion-proof electrical components, coatings, and software (SLAM, point cloud processing, target recognition, path planning, digital twins, process simulation, spray parameter databases)
- Midstream: integration into autonomous mobile robots, wall-climbing robots, suspended robots, aerial platforms, and adaptive industrial spraying workstations
- Downstream: building contractors, professional coating service providers, shipyards, shipowners, tank operators, wind turbine manufacturers/operators, automotive repair networks, and industrial manufacturers

**Market Segmentation:**
- Platform types: autonomous mobile manipulators (broadest applicability), magnetic adsorption wall-climbing robots (steel tanks, ships, towers), fixed/rail/gantry scan-generated trajectory systems, rope-suspended and aerial platforms
- Programming methods: 3D scan-generated trajectories and vision-based automatic planning expected to expand; teaching/learning remains suitable for industrial clients not wanting major production layout changes
- Downstream: construction, ship maintenance, oil & gas storage/transport, wind power, auto refinishing, and flexible industrial manufacturing

**Regional Analysis:**
- Europe: largest supply region (39%), strong in self-learning industrial spraying, tank/ship coating, wind power robot services, and professional construction robots
- China: ~27%, broadest manufacturer base covering construction, auto refinishing, wall-climbing platforms, wind power parts, and general industrial spraying, but with varying product maturity, financial transparency, and export capability
- North America: ~20%, emphasizing RaaS and robot construction contracting models
- Israel: specialized in construction robotics; India and Southeast Asia at early stages driven by construction decoration robot startups; Japan, Korea, and Taiwan have strong traditional robot/automation bases but limited independent product sales under this report's autonomy definition

**Competitive Landscape:**
- Application-specialization-driven fragmented structure; no single standard product dominates all scenarios
- Tier 1: suppliers with real equipment, repeat customer projects, proprietary perception/path-planning capabilities, and field delivery resources (some commercialized through wind power, construction, or large-asset robot service)
- Tier 2: focused on auto refinishing, shipyards, tanks, construction decoration, and large industrial workpieces
- Chinese manufacturers: advantages in cost, customization speed, and domestic engineering support
- European companies: leading in specialized coating processes, mature industrial channels, and high-value asset applications
- North American companies: developing per-project billing and RaaS recurring revenue models

**Key Companies Mentioned (20):** Aerones Inc., PaintJet Inc., 埃夫特智能机器人股份有限公司 (EFORT Intelligent Equipment), Qlayers B.V., Okibo Ltd., 浙江史河科技有限公司 (Zhejiang Shihe Technology), Lesta s.r.l., 广东博智林机器人有限公司 (Guangdong Bright Dream Robotics), Epistolio S.r.l., 武汉湾流科技股份有限公司 (Wuhan Bayflow Technology), Ventherm A/S, Tebulo Robotics, Apellix LLC, ConBotics GmbH, 深圳领鹊科技有限公司 (Shenzhen Lingque Technology), AMBPR SAS, 清研同创机器人（天津）有限公司 (Tsingyan Tongchuang Robotics Tianjin), Finish Robotics, Eternal Robotics, 深圳市行知行机器人技术有限公司 (Shenzhen Xingzhixing Robot Technology)

**Report Structure Overview (8 Sections):**
1. Executive summary with core findings
2. Global supply and demand analysis with historical data to 2032 forecasts
3. Competitive landscape analysis (CR4, CR8 concentration metrics)
4. Key country market comparison (US vs. China in depth)
5. Segment deep-dive analysis (by product type: autonomous mobile manipulators, magnetic adsorption wall-climbing robots, aerial spraying robots, others; by application: construction/building services, shipbuilding/offshore, oil & gas, others)
6. Company-level deep research profiles
7. Industry chain analysis (upstream materials/components to downstream sales channels)
8. Research conclusions and outlook

The report is produced by 环洋市场咨询 (Global Info Research) and covers the 2021-2032 period.

--- SOURCE 1: 离散制造行业数字化转型与智能化升级路径研究Paths for the ... ---
URL: http://devp-service.oss-cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com/6d18b64cc1bb458bba8cdc05a7104113/file_1649924225561.pdf

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This paper (published in Strategic Study of CAE/中国工程科学, 2022, Vol. 24, No. 2) by Li Xinyu, Li Zhaofu, and Gao Liang of Huazhong University of Science and Technology examines the digital transformation and intelligent upgrade paths for China's discrete manufacturing industry. 

**Typical Characteristics of Discrete Manufacturing:** The article identifies nine characteristics including: diverse sub-sectors with significant differences in application base, market demand, and business models; full product lifecycle dimensions (R&D, production, sales, operations, recycling); process flows based on order/inventory production with multi-variety, small-batch or single-piece manufacturing; low automation levels requiring quality checks on each part and process; frequently changing process routes; batch number management and tracking; job scheduling based on priority and equipment capacity; manual data collection supplemented by barcode scanning; and equipment management where multiple machines can perform the same process.

**Challenges Facing Transformation:** Five major challenges are identified: (1) weak application foundation due to unbalanced digitalization and informatization; (2) lack of key technologies with heavy dependence on imported industrial equipment and software; (3) shortage of talent and cultural resources; (4) difficulties in data aggregation and utilization due to diverse protocols, incomplete collection, and security concerns; and (5) unclear economic benefits, especially for SMEs facing high transformation costs and low returns.

**Common Key Technologies:** The paper covers three categories: (1) Advanced manufacturing technologies including intelligent design (with topology optimization for weight reduction, metamaterial design for negative Poisson's ratio and thermal invisibility), intelligent processing, intelligent scheduling (including 5G-enabled workshop scheduling), and intelligent inspection; (2) New-generation information technologies including 5G, edge computing, and blockchain for connecting "digital islands" and enabling human-machine interaction; (3) New-generation AI technologies including deep learning for fault diagnosis and surface defect detection (semi-supervised CNNs, multi-representation domain adaptation networks).

**Four Case Studies (with timeline tables):**

**Key themes:**
- Discrete and batch manufacturers typically run hundreds of computing applications (ERP supported by IT, automation/MES by OT, and many custom Excel/Access/Java apps that are poorly supported).

- MES/MOM systems should provide visibility, control, and traceability across six manufacturing elements: materials, equipment, labor, tooling/containers, suppliers, and data.

**LNS Research's advice for manufacturers:**
1. No vendor has grasped the Grail yet; a proven solution is more than five years away.

3. IX Platforms can deliver significant value by "wrapping and extending" MES systems.

**Key Differences:**
- **Discrete Manufacturing**: Produces distinct, countable items (cars, aircraft, electronics) that can be disassembled into original components. Uses complex, multi-level Bills of Materials (BOMs), quality control per unit, and offers high customization. Industries include automotive, aerospace, and electronics.
- **Process Manufacturing**: Transforms raw materials through chemical, biological, or physical processes into finished products that cannot be disassembled (chemicals, beverages, processed foods). **Benefits and Challenges:**
- Discrete manufacturing offers high customization but creates complex supply chains and inventory management challenges.

1. Understand your product's nature (complexity, volume, customization)
2. Consider the manufacturing method—discrete suits assembled products needing flexibility; process suits homogeneous, standardized production
3. Evaluate software capabilities (BOM tracking for discrete; formula/batch management for process)
4. Check for specialized features (advanced planning/scheduling for discrete; process control and real-time monitoring for process)

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is a comprehensive survey paper titled "Embodied Intelligence for Flexible Manufacturing: A Survey" (面向柔性制造的具身智能综述), authored by XU Kai (National University of Defense Technology), ZHAO Hang (Wuhan University), HU Ruizhen (Shenzhen University), YANG Min (Hunan University), LIU Hao and ZHANG Hui (Hunan University), and YU Haibin (Shenyang Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences). The paper was published in April 2025 (volume 47, number 4, DOI: 250208) and funded by multiple Chinese national science foundations including the National Natural Science Foundation of China (62325211, 62132021, 62322207, 92148204, 62433010, 62303174) and other provincial and national programs.

**Core Thesis and Contributions:**
- Embodied intelligence is rapidly penetrating industrial manufacturing due to advances in AI (DeepSeek, GPT-4). Industrial scenarios—with semi-structured environments, stable conditions, and standardized processes—are poised to be the first domain for large-scale embodied intelligence adoption.
- The shift toward high-productivity, small-batch flexible manufacturing creates new normal conditions: mixed-model production lines, rapid product iterations, and unstructured non-standard processes. This poses three core challenges: (1) accurate process modeling/monitoring under limited sensing, (2) maintaining dynamic balance between flexible adaptation and high-precision manipulation, and (3) coordinating general robotic skills with specialized industrial procedures.

**Organizing Framework — "Industrial Eye - Industrial Hand - Industrial Brain" (工业之眼-工业之手-工业之脑):**

**Part 1: Industrial Eye (Perception Layer)** covers multimodal data fusion and real-time modeling:
- 3D vision high-precision imaging: structured light (sub-millimeter precision, 0.1-5m range), Time-of-Flight (cm-level precision, 0.1-10m), and multi-view RGB imaging (cm-level, 0.5-50m). Methods include Fourier Transform Profilometry, Phase-Shifting Profilometry, Phase Measuring Deflectometry (for high-reflection surfaces), line-scan cameras, KinectFusion, MIPS-Fusion, GeoTransformer, COLMAP, NeRF, Gaussian Splatting, and emerging foundation models DUSt3R and VGGT.
- Defect detection and dimensional measurement: 3D vision enables micro-meter to sub-millimeter precision (e.g., ±0.2mm non-contact measurement, reconstruction error <0.05mm for complex engine housings). Case studies include automotive paint surface reconstruction via PMD (reducing false-negative rates to <1%, false-positive to <3%) and ship welding with FoundationStereo achieving ±0.2mm depth reconstruction.
- Multi-source data fusion: covers RGB, depth/point cloud, acoustic, infrared, and force-torque modalities. Feature extraction uses ResNet, ViT, PointNet++, Point Transformer, 1D CNN, TCN, GRU. Pretrained models (MAE, DINOv2, PointMAE, PTv3, PANNs, TimesNet) reduce training costs. Alignment via contrastive learning (CLIP), joint embedding, and attention mechanisms (MulT, EMT, AnyGPT, TEAL, Meta-Transformer). Fusion strategies include early, late, and intermediate fusion with trade-offs.
- Industrial vision foundation models: self-supervised learning (MIM, contrastive learning, teacher-student frameworks like DINO), SAM/SAM 2 for segmentation, Depth Anything for depth estimation, FoundationPose for 6D pose, 3D-VisTA and UniT3D for 3D tasks. Fine-tuning via full fine-tuning, linear probing, and PEFT (LoRA, Adapter Tuning, Prompt Tuning). Case studies include AnomalyDINO for few-shot defect detection and DUSt3R for low-texture image matching.

**Part 2: Industrial Hand (Control Layer)** covers flexible adaptive precise manipulation:
- Low-precision hardware control: pose recognition (DOPE, SOCS, MIRETR for cluttered scenes), control strategies comparing traditional model-driven (PID, LQR, fuzzy logic), imitation learning, reinforcement learning, and IL+RL hybrids (Deepmimic, AMP, residual policies). Sim2Real transfer via domain randomization, Gaussian Splatting (SplatSim, RobogSim, ManiGaussian, PIN-WM). Case studies: Tsinghua's digital-twin + residual policy for 3C assembly, and Stanford's ALOHA system achieving millimeter-level dual-arm manipulation on <$20K hardware (success rate improved from 60% to 96%, cycle time reduced 30-40%).
- Flexible operation for variable production lines: policy distillation (AutoMate achieving >80% average success across 80 assembly tasks, 86.5% on 20 real parts), meta-learning (ODA for insertion tasks), interaction representations (affordance, IBS for dexterous grasping, DP3), and decision foundation models (Palm-E, SayCan, Embodied-GPT, OpenVLA trained on 970K demonstrations, π0.5, ConRFT achieving 96.3% average success with 45-90 min fine-tuning). Case studies: NVIDIA's universal assembly policy and RoboGrind LLM-guided grinding system.
- Adaptive process parameter regulation for welding (CNN/MLP-based molten pool width control, RL-based laser power control), grinding (IPSO-GRNN for surface roughness prediction, MAML-PPOBE meta-RL achieving superior material removal accuracy), and assembly (RL-based rotor assembly, vision-force bolt fastening, visual servoing with disturbance observers).

**Part 3: Industrial Brain (Decision Layer)** covers process planning and line scheduling:
- Factory scheduling: Job Shop Scheduling Problem (JSSP) via traditional methods (branch-and-bound, genetic algorithms, simulated annealing, tabu search) and learning-based approaches (GIN-based reinforcement learning, multi-agent RL with PPO, LLM-based auto algorithm design like SeEvo). Multi-AGV path planning (TSP/VRP) using RL, transformer attention (AM), and diffusion solvers (DIFUSCO, DISCO). Online bin packing via deep RL (CDRL, PCT for continuous 3D online packing, TAP-Net for joint order and position optimization).
- Digital twin for virtual-physical synchronization: state perception, synchronization, and twin-based intelligent scheduling for enhanced flexibility and responsiveness.

**Key Challenges and Data Points:**
- Assembly precision requirements: ±0.05mm (auto assembly), 0.1-0.5mm gaps; grinding: Ra ≤0.8μm, shape error ±0.2mm (wind blades), ±0.03mm (aero-engine blades); welding: ±0.2 to ±0.5mm standard tracking, ±0.1-0.2mm for precision applications.
- Ship welding accounts for ~40% of hull construction costs; automotive paint defect detection traditionally has 15-20% false detection rates and >30% miss rates under fatigue.

**Future Outlook:** The paper proposes a three-stage evolution model for embodied intelligence in flexible manufacturing: "cognition enhancement → skill transition → system evolution" (认知增强-技能跃迁-系统进化), and discusses humanoid robots covering eye-hand-brain capabilities. It focuses on discrete manufacturing (not process manufacturing) and provides a theoretical framework and practical reference for cross-disciplinary industrial embodied intelligence development.
</summary>

The article discusses how tactile sensing is becoming a key "new infrastructure" for robotic dexterity and enabling flexible manufacturing transformation.

Key points covered:
1. **The problem**: Traditional industrial robots rely on extreme positioning accuracy and visual guidance, but fail in flexible production tasks (e.g., automotive wiring harnesses, flexible sealing strips) where material deformation and positional deviations create unpredictable contact "black boxes." Robots often fail as "blind operators" in these scenarios.

2. **The solution**: Yimu Technology's visual-tactile sensors convert raw visual signals captured by photosensitive elements into machine-understandable "tactile" intelligence. The sensor's flexible contact surface uses a micro-optical system to capture microscopic deformation images during contact, which are then analyzed through AI algorithms into high-density pressure distribution, shear force, contact geometry, and other multi-dimensional mechanical information.

3. **Paradigm shift**: The control paradigm moves from "preset path, avoid contact" to "perceive contact, intelligently comply" — closer to human operation logic and solving automation challenges in complex work segments that depend on "hand feel."

4. **Product matrix**: Unlike many lab-stage tactile sensing solutions, Yimu Technology has built a complete product lineup covering square, wedge, fingertip, and pinky-finger forms, adapted to different gripping configurations and installation scenarios. Engineering challenges overcome include material durability, batch production consistency, and environmental robustness.

5. **Demonstration**: At the expo, a robotic arm with the sensor smoothly completed high-precision insertion tasks. When slight positional deviations existed, the arm used real-time contact force and micro-slip feedback signals for local adaptive adjustment, achieving "one-time alignment, compliant insertion."

6. **Strategic value**: Tactile sensing reduces dependence on upstream absolute positioning accuracy, lowers system complexity and integration costs, and enables true production line flexibility (reducing reprogramming and debugging time during frequent product changeovers). Yimu is exploring a "visual-tactile-language-action" multimodal embodied closed-loop framework, noting that tactile data—unlike visual and language data available from the internet—must be generated through real physical interaction, making it a high-barrier strategic asset and potential competitive moat.

# 《世界机器人2025》报告：全球工业机器人发展格局

供稿人：陈莹供稿时间：2025-10-27 10:59:33关键词：工业机器人,机器人,自动化,数字化

2025 年 9 月 25 日，国际机器人联合会（IFR）发布《2025 年世界机器人报告》，报告详细分析了全球工业机器人的市场状况。

报告中工业机器人统计数据显示，2024 年全球新增工业机器人装机量达 54.2 万台，较 10 年前增长超一倍。这是全球工业机器人年度装机量连续第四年突破 50 万台。2024 年，亚洲地区占全球新增装机量的 74%，欧洲和美洲则分别占 16% 和 9%。国际机器人联合会主席Takayuki Ito表示："《世界机器人》最新统计数据表明，2024年工业机器人年度安装量创下历史第二高纪录，仅比两年前的峰值低2%。众多行业向数字化和自动化时代转型，带来了需求的巨大增长。2024年，全球在役工业机器人总数达到466.4万台，较上年增长9%。"

报告从亚洲、欧洲、美洲三个关键市场区域进行了阐述和分析，具体内容如下：

一、亚洲

2024年，中国仍然是全球最大的工业机器人市场，占全球新增安装量的54%。最新数据显示，中国新安装了29.5万台工业机器人，创下年度最高纪录。中国本土制造商在国内市场的销量首次超过了外资供应商。去年，本土品牌的国内市场份额从过去十年约 28% 的水平攀升至 57%。中国的在役机器人存量在2024年突破了200万台大关，规模位居各国之首。随着中国机器人产业不断开拓新市场，目前没有迹象表明中国的机器人需求会下降。直到2028年，中国制造业的机器人需求仍具有巨大潜力，预计每年平均增长可达10%。

日本保持了保持全球第二大工业机器人市场的地位，2024年新增安装量为4.45万台，小幅下降4%，其在役机器人存量增长了3%，目前有45.05万在使用。2025年，日本机器人需求将以较低的个位数增长率小幅增长。随后几年，平均增长率将加速至中等水平。

2024 年，韩国工业机器人新增装机量为 3.06 万台，下降3%。自2019年以来，其年度安装量一直在3.1万台左右徘徊。就2024年年度安装量而言，韩国是全球第四大机器人市场，排在美国、日本和中国之后。

印度工业机器人市场持续增长，2024年安装量创下9,100台的新纪录，同比增长7%。汽车行业是最大驱动因素，占印度机器人市场份额的 45%。在年度安装量方面，印度位居全球第六，仅次于德国。

二、欧洲

2024年，欧洲的工业机器人安装量下降8%，降至8.5万台，但这一数值仍是历史第二高。欧洲所有机器人安装量的80%发生在欧盟内部（6.78万台）。欧洲的机器人需求受益于近岸外包趋势，2019年至2024年的年平均增长率为3%。

德国是欧洲最大、全球第五大机器人市场。2024年安装量下降5%，降至26,982台，德国是欧洲最大、全球第五大机器人市场，占欧洲年度总量的32%。欧洲第二大市场意大利的安装量下降了16%，至8,783台。西班牙目前排名第三（新增5,100台），汽车行业需求强劲。法国（新增4,900台）降至第四位，降幅达24%。在英国，2024年工业机器人安装量下降35%，至2,500台。2023年创纪录的3,800台是一次性高峰，由已于2023年第一季度结束的"超级扣除"税收抵免计划推动。过去十年，英国的安装量呈周期性波动。2024年，英国机器人安装量在全球排名第19位。

三、美洲

美洲的机器人安装量连续第四年超过5万台：2024年安装了50,100台，较2023年水平下降10%。

美国作为该地区最大的市场，在2024年占美洲安装量的68%。机器人安装量下降9%，至3.42万台。美国的大部分机器人从日本和欧洲进口，本土供应商数量较少，但国内拥有大量机器人系统集成商，负责落地机器人自动化解决方案。墨西哥2024年总安装量达到5,600台，下降4%。汽车行业仍然是墨西哥工业机器人的核心需求领域，2024 年占该国机器人总装机量的 63%。在加拿大，机器人安装量下降12%，至3,800台。加拿大的安装数据很大程度上依赖于汽车行业的投资周期。2024年，2024 年汽车行业占该国机器人装机量的 47%。

四、展望

经济合作与发展组织（OECD）和国际货币基金组织（IMF）预测，2025 年全球经济增长率将处于 2.9% 至 3.0% 之间，2026 年则将在 2.9% 至 3.1% 之间。然而，地缘政治紧张局势、东欧与中东地区的暴力冲突以及贸易受阻等因素，正对全球经济产生负面影响。机器人产业无法免受全球宏观经济环境的影响，但目前尚无迹象表明其整体长期增长趋势会在短期内终止。尽管不同地区的发展趋势差异显著，但全球机器人产业的总体发展轨迹仍保持向好。从全球范围来看，2025 年机器人新增装机量预计将增长 6%，达到 57.5 万台；到 2028 年，这一数值将突破 70 万台大关。

args.summary:
This webpage reports on the International Federation of Robotics (IFR) "World Robotics 2025" report, released on September 25, 2025, which analyzes the global industrial robot market landscape. Key findings include:

**Global Overview:**
- In 2024, global new industrial robot installations reached 542,000 units, more than double the figure from 10 years ago. This marks the fourth consecutive year of exceeding 500,000 annual installations.
- Asia accounted for 74% of global new installations in 2024, with Europe at 16% and the Americas at 9%.
- The total global operational stock of industrial robots reached 4.664 million units in 2024, up 9% year-over-year.
- 2024's annual installation figure was the second-highest in history, only 2% below the peak two years prior.

**Asia:**
- China remained the world's largest industrial robot market, accounting for 54% of global new installations (295,000 units in 2024, a record high). For the first time, domestic Chinese manufacturers outsold foreign suppliers in the domestic market, with local brands' domestic market share jumping from ~28% over the past decade to 57% in 2024. China's operational robot stock surpassed 2 million units, the largest of any country. Chinese manufacturing robot demand is expected to grow at an average of 10% annually through 2028.
- Japan remained the second-largest market with 44,500 new installations in 2024 (down 4%), with operational stock of 450,500 units (up 3%). Japan's robot demand is expected to grow at low single-digit rates in 2025.
- South Korea installed 30,600 units in 2024 (down 3%), ranking as the world's fourth-largest market.
- India set a record with 9,100 installations (up 7%), driven primarily by the automotive sector (45% market share). India ranked sixth globally.

**Europe:**
- European installations fell 8% to 85,000 units in 2024 (still the second-highest historically). 80% of European installations (67,800 units) occurred within the EU. European demand benefited from nearshoring trends, with 3% average annual growth from 2019-2024.
- Germany was Europe's largest and globally fifth-largest market with 26,982 installations (down 5%), representing 32% of Europe's total.
- Italy: 8,783 installations (down 16%); Spain: 5,100 (third in Europe, strong automotive demand); France: 4,900 (down 24%, fell to fourth); UK: 2,500 (down 35%, 19th globally). The UK's 2023 record of 3,800 was a one-time peak driven by a "super deduction" tax credit program that ended in Q1 2023.

**Americas:**
- The Americas exceeded 50,000 installations for the fourth consecutive year with 50,100 units in 2024 (down 10%).
- The US was the region's largest market, accounting for 68% of installations with 34,200 units (down 9%). The US imports most robots from Japan and Europe but has many domestic system integrators.
- Mexico: 5,600 installations (down 4%), with automotive industry accounting for 63% of installations.
- Canada: 3,800 installations (down 12%), with automotive sector at 47%.

**Outlook:**
- OECD and IMF forecast global economic growth of 2.9-3.0% in 2025 and 2.9-3.1% in 2026, despite geopolitical tensions and conflicts in Eastern Europe and the Middle East.
- Global robot installations are projected to grow 6% in 2025 to 575,000 units, surpassing 700,000 units by 2028.
- Despite regional differences, the overall long-term growth trajectory of the global robotics industry remains positive.

The report was contributed by Chen Ying on October 27, 2025, and references two IFR sources from September 25, 2025.

# Best-of **World Robotics 2025**

 

## Top Facts Summary

The International Federation of Robotics (IFR) published the World Robotics 2025 data on September 25th. The annual report provides global statistics on [industrial robots](#industrial-robots) and [service robots](#service-robots).

[Industrial Robots](#industrial-robots) [Service Robots](#service-robots) [Press Photo Gallery](#press-photos)

---

### Industrial Robots

* 542,000 industrial robots were installed in 2024, more than double the number from 10 years ago. Annual installations topped 500,000 units for the fourth straight year.
* Asia accounted for 74% of new deployments in 2024, compared with 16% in Europe and 9% in the Americas.

* **China** is by far the world’s largest market in 2024, representing 54% of global deployments. The latest figures show that 295,000 industrial robots have been installed - the highest annual total on record. For the first time, Chinese manufacturers have sold more than foreign suppliers in their home country. Their domestic market share climbed to 57% last year, up from about 28% over the past decade. China’s operational robot stock exceeded the 2 million mark in 2024, the largest of any country. As robotics in China is opening up new markets, there is no indication that robot demand in China will decrease. There is still a lot of potential in Chinese manufacturing for 10% growth on average each year until 2028.
* **Japan** maintained its position as the second-largest market for industrial robots, with 44,500 units installed in 2024 – a slight 4% decrease. The country's operational stock rose by 3%, with 450,500 units now in use. Demand for robots will grow slightly by lower single-digit rates in 2025. It will then accelerate to a medium single-digit rate on average in the next few years.
* The market in the **Republic of Korea:** installed 30,600 units in 2024 – down 3%. Annual installations had been trending sideways of around 31,000 units since 2019. The country is the fourth largest robot market in the world in terms of annual installations in 2024, after the United States, Japan, and China.
* **India** continues to grow with a record of 9,100 units installed in 2024 – up 7%. The automotive industry was the strongest driver with a market share of 45%. In terms of annual installations, India ranks sixth worldwide, one place up behind Germany.

#### [Europe](#collapse-europe)

* Industrial robot installations in **Europe** fell 8% to 85,000 units in 2024, still the second largest number recorded in history. 80% of all European robot installations took place in the European Union (67,800 units). Robot demand in Europe benefited from the nearshoring trend. The annual average growth rate from 2019 to 2024 was plus 3%.
* **Germany** is the largest robot market in Europe and the fifth-largest in the world. Installations fell 5% to 26,982 units in 2024, which is the second-best result recorded after the record year of 2023. This represents a 32% market share of the annual total in Europe.
* The number of installations in **Italy**, the second largest European market, fell by 16% to 8,783 units.
* **Spain** is now in third place (5,100 units), with a strong demand from the automotive industry.
* **France** (4,900 units) moved down to fourth place, with a 24% decrease.
* In the **UK**, industrial robot installations were down 35% to 2,500 units in 2024. The record number of 3,800 units in 2023 was a one-off peak, driven by the “super-deduction” tax credit program, which ended after the first quarter of 2023. Installation counts moved sideways with some cyclicity over the past decade. Robot installations in the UK rank 19th worldwide in 2024.

#### [The Americas](#collapse-americas)

* Robot installations in the **Americas** exceeded 50,000 units for the fourth year in a row: 50,100 units were installed in 2024, down 10% below the level reached 2023.
* The **United States**, the largest regional market, accounted for 68% of installations in the Americas in 2024. Robot installations were down by 9% to 34,200 units. The United States imports most of its robots from Japan and Europe, with few domestic suppliers. However, there are numerous domestic robot system integrators implementing robotic automation solutions.
* Total installations in **Mexico** reached 5,600 units in 2024, a decrease of 4%. The automotive industry remained the key customer of industrial robots in Mexico, accounting for 63% of the installations in 2024.
* In **Canada**, robot installations declined by 12% to 3,800 units. Installation figures in Canada largely depend on automotive investment cycles. The share of the car industry was 47% in 2024.

### Service Robots

#### [Global](#collapse-global2)

* The total number of service robots sold for professional use reached almost 200,000 units in 2024, marking a 9% increase.
* Staff shortages are a key driver for companies to use robots designed for trained professionals.
* The growing elderly population is increasing demand for medical robots.

#### [Professional Service Robots](#collapse-service)

* With 102,900 units (+14%) sold in 2024, more than every other professional service robot was built for the application class **transportation and logistics**. These robots cover mainly mobile robots for the transport and handling of goods. While traditional sales remained the main channel of monetarization, RaaS enjoyed growing popularity with a growth rate of 42% in 2024. Transportation in **indoor environments without public traffic** qualifies as the most important application class within this segment. A special chapter in World Robotics 2025 focuses on the drivers and challenges in this dynamic market.
* **Hospitality robots** remain second place with more than 42,000 sold – down 11%. Robots for mobile guidance, information points in public environments and telepresence account for the majority of these robots. Such service robots are taking over small services or promoting sales in stores, shopping malls, or at front desks. As the sector is evolving, new applications have emerged, such as food and beverage preparation.
* The market for **professional cleaning robots**, in third place, grew by 34% to more than 25,000 units sold. The main application is floor cleaning.
* Sales of **agricultural robots** rank fourth and contracted slightly by 6% with close to 19,500 units sold. The decrease was mainly driven by cultivation and milking.
* For the application group of **search & rescue, security robots** a total number of 3,100 units were sold in 2024, placing it in fifth position up 19%. Three out of four robots in this application class were for security services.

#### [Medical Robots](#collapse-medical)

In accordance with ISO standard the World Robotics 2025 yearbook considers **medical robots** as a third category alongside service robots and industrial robots:

* Sales of medical robots increased strongly by 91% to around 16,700 units in 2024.
* Sales of **rehabilitation and non-invasive therapy robots** were up 106%.
* Demand for **surgery** robots rose by 41% and sales of robots for **diagnostics and medical laboratory analysis** increased by 610%.

#### [Consumer Service Robots](#collapse-consumer)

* **Consumer service robots** are produced for the mass market.
* Service robots for consumer use have experienced a solid growth rate of 11% with close to 20 million units sold in 2024.
* Robots for **domestic tasks** (floor cleaning, lawn moving etc.) were by far the largest group of consumer robots.
* Growth was largely driven by companies from Europe and Asia-Pacific, which both experienced growth rates of 16%, whereas sales from the Americas decreased by 1%. This was due to a loss in the market share for robotic vacuum cleaners.

#### [Humanoid Robots](#collapse-humanoid)

IFR's Position Paper "Humanoid Robots" is available as a free download:

<https://ifr.org/papers>

**Note on Service Robot Data**  
 World Robotics Service Robots is based on sample data and is not projected to the entire industry. Sample composition varies each year. The 2025 report is based on a sample of 294 service robot suppliers. **Compiling or comparing data from different World Robotics Reports is strongly discouraged.**

* 发布机构：国际机器人联合会（IFR）
* 发布人：国际机器人联合会（IFR）
* 发布时间：2024-10
* 报告类型： 行业
* 关键词：机器人行业,安装量,2024年,研究报告
* 报告摘要：

  2024年9月24日，国际机器人联合会（IFR）发布《2024年全球机器人报告》。根据报告，截至2023年底，全球工厂中运行的机器人已达4281585台，同比增长%。年安装量连续第三年超过50万台。按地区划分，2023年，有新部署的机器人中有70%安装在亚洲，17%安装在欧洲，10%安装在美洲。

  国际机器人联合会主席玛丽娜·比尔表示：“新的世界机器人统计数据显示，全球用于自动化生产的工业机器人数量创历史新高。2023年的年安装量为541302台，创历史第二高，比2022年安装的552946台创纪录的安装量仅低2%。”

  **亚洲地区**

  中国是迄今为止世界上最大的市场。2023年，中国安装的工业机器人数量为276288台，占全球安装量的51%。这一结果是有史以来第二高的水平（2022年为290144台）。自2022年以来，中国制造商在国内市场的份额大幅增长，2023年达到47%。在过去十年中，这一比例一直在28%左右波动。2023年，运营库存略低于180万台大关，使中国成为世界上第一个也是唯一一个拥有如此庞大机器人库存的国家。预计机器人需求将在2024年下半年加速，到年底市场将更加稳定。从长远来看，中国制造业仍有很大的增长潜力，到2027年，年均增长率有望达到5-10%。

  日本仍然是全球第二大工业机器人市场，仅次于中国。2023年机器人安装量达到46106台，同比下降9%。此前两年表现强劲，2022年达到峰值50435台，仅次于2018年（55240台）。预计2024年机器人需求将保持停滞，但2025年及随后几年将恢复至中等和较高的个位数增长率。

  韩国市场呈现横向趋势：2023年安装量达到31444台，同比下降1%。按年安装量计算，该国是全球第四大机器人市场，仅次于美国、日本和中国。

  印度是增长最快的亚洲新兴经济体之一。2023年机器人安装量同比增长59%，达到8510台，创下新高。汽车行业的需求飙升至3551台，增幅达139%。汽车制造商和供应商都为这一发展做出了贡献。

  **欧洲地区**

  欧洲工业机器人安装量同比增长9%，达到92393台的新高。总体而言，2023年80%的安装量可归因于欧盟目的地（73534台，+2%）。延迟的项目已完成，积压订单已在2023年清理完毕。该地区的机器人需求也受益于近岸外包趋势。2023年，汽车行业投资于传统汽车制造强国（如西班牙，5053台，+31%），同时也投资于斯洛伐克（2174台，+48%）或匈牙利（1657台，+31%）等较小的市场，这有力地推动了增长。

  作为欧洲最大的市场，且是全球前五大市场中唯一的欧洲市场，德国的安装量同比增长7%，达到28355台。欧洲第二大市场意大利的安装量同比下降9%，达到10412台。欧洲第三大市场法国的安装量同比下降13%，为6386台。

  在英国，2023年工业机器人安装量同比增长51%，达到3830台。投资主要由汽车行业的安装推动，主要用于装配任务。

  **美洲地区**

  美洲的机器人安装量连续第三年超过5万台：2023年安装了55389台，仅比2022年创下的历史最高水平低1%。

  美国是最大的区域市场，占2023年美洲安装量的68%。机器人安装量同比下降5%至37587台，这是继2022年和2018年之后的第三高纪录。汽车行业的需求同比下降15%至12421台。与过去十年的平均水平一致。金属和机械行业的安装量增长8%至4171台。美国电气/电子行业的安装量保持稳定在3900台（+1%）。

  在加拿大，机器人安装量同比增长37%，达到4311台。加拿大的安装量很大程度上取决于汽车投资周期。2023年汽车行业的份额为58%。

  墨西哥的机器人需求主要来自汽车行业，该行业占据了70%的市场份额：该行业的安装量同比下降5%，至4087台，显示出该客户群体中众所周知的周期性需求模式。2023年总安装量达到5832台，同比下降3%。

  **未来前景**

  经合组织预计全球经济增长将趋于稳定。然而，地缘政治逆风仍被视为主要风险和不确定因素。最近的危机提高了政治层面对战略产业国内生产能力的认识。自动化使制造商能够在不牺牲成本效率的情况下将生产设在发达经济体。到2024年，全球经济衰退将触底。全球机器人安装量预计将稳定在54.1万台。预计增长将在2025年加速，并在2026年和2027年持续。没有迹象表明整体长期增长趋势将在近期结束。

This webpage from the CMES (China Mechanical Engineering Society) library presents the International Federation of Robotics (IFR) "World Robotics 2024 Report," released on September 24, 2024. The report reveals that by the end of 2023, a record 4,281,585 robots were operating in factories worldwide. Annual installations exceeded 500,000 units for the third consecutive year, with 541,302 units installed in 2023 (the second-highest ever, just 2% below the 2022 record of 552,946). Regional distribution of new installations in 2023: 70% in Asia, 17% in Europe, and 10% in the Americas.

KEY REGIONAL HIGHLIGHTS:

Asia: China remains the world's largest robot market, installing 276,288 units in 2023 (51% of global installations), with Chinese manufacturers' domestic market share growing to 47% (up from ~28% over the past decade). China's operational stock approached 1.8 million units, making it the first and only country with such a large robot inventory. Demand is expected to accelerate in H2 2024, with annual growth of 5-10% projected through 2027. Japan (2nd largest market) installed 46,106 units (-9% YoY, down from the 2022 peak of 50,435). Korea installed 31,444 units (-1% YoY, 4th largest market). India was the fastest-growing Asian economy, with installations surging 59% to 8,510 units, driven by automotive demand which grew 139% to 3,551 units.

Europe: European installations rose 9% to a record 92,393 units, with 80% going to EU destinations (73,534 units, +2%). Nearshoring trends and completed backlogged projects drove growth, particularly in automotive investments in Spain (5,053 units, +31%), Slovakia (2,174 units, +48%), and Hungary (1,657 units, +31%). Germany (Europe's largest market) grew 7% to 28,355 units; Italy fell 9% to 10,412 units; France fell 13% to 6,386 units; the UK grew 51% to 3,830 units driven by automotive assembly.

Americas: Regional installations exceeded 50,000 units for the third consecutive year at 55,389 units (1% below the 2022 record). The US accounted for 68% of regional installations (37,587 units, -5% YoY), with automotive demand down 15% to 12,421 units, metal/machinery up 8% to 4,171 units, and electrical/electronics stable at 3,900 units. Canada grew 37% to 4,311 units (58% automotive share). Mexico's total fell 3% to 5,832 units, with automotive accounting for 70% of demand.

Future Outlook: OECD expects global economic growth to stabilize; while geopolitical headwinds remain key risks, recent crises raised political awareness of domestic production capacity in strategic industries. Automation enables manufacturers to maintain production in developed economies without sacrificing cost efficiency. Global economic recession is expected to bottom out in 2024, with robot installations projected to stabilize at 541,000 units. Growth is expected to accelerate in 2025 and continue through 2026-2027, with no indication of an end to the long-term growth trend.

# World Robotics 2025 report – INDUSTRIAL ROBOTS – released by IFR

### Global Robot Demand in Factories Doubles Over 10 Years

_Frankfurt, Sep 25, 2025 —_ The new World Robotics 2025 statistics on industrial robots showed 542,000 robots installed in 2024 - more than double the number 10 years ago. Annual installations topped 500,000 units for the fourth straight year. Asia accounted for 74% of new deployments in 2024, compared with 16% in Europe and 9% in the Americas. 

![Image 2](https://ifr.org/downloads/press_docs/Teaser_global_market_2014_-_2024.jpg)

“The new World Robotics statistics show 2024 the second highest annual installation count of industrial robots in history - only 2% lower than the all-time-high two years ago,” says Takayuki Ito, President of the International Federation of Robotics. “The transition of many industries into the digital and automated age has been marked by a huge surge in demand. The total number of industrial robots in operational use worldwide was 4,664,000 units in 2024 – an increase of 9% compared to the previous year.”

## Asia, Europe and the Americas - overview

**China**is by far the world’s largest market in 2024, representing 54% of global deployments. The latest figures show that 295,000 industrial robots have been installed - the highest annual total on record. For the first time, Chinese manufacturers have sold more than foreign suppliers in their home country. Their domestic market share climbed to 57% last year, up from about 28% over the past decade. China’s operational robot stock exceeded the 2 million mark in 2024, the largest of any country. As robotics in China is opening up new markets, there is no indication that robot demand in China will decrease. There is still a lot of potential in Chinese manufacturing for 10% growth on average each year until 2028.

**Japan**maintained its position as the second-largest market for industrial robots, with 44,500 units installed in 2024 – a slight 4% decrease. The country's operational stock rose by 3%, with 450,500 units now in use. Demand for robots will grow slightly by lower single-digit rates in 2025. It will then accelerate to a medium single-digit rate on average in the next few years.

The market in the **Republic of Korea** installed 30,600 units in 2024 – down 3%. Annual installations had been trending sideways of around 31,000 units since 2019. The country is the fourth largest robot market in the world in terms of annual installations in 2024, after the United States, Japan, and China.

**India**continues to grow with a record of 9,100 units installed in 2024 – up 7%. The automotive industry was the strongest driver with a market share of 45%. In terms of annual installations, India ranks sixth worldwide, one place up behind Germany.

## Europe

Industrial robot installations in **Europe**fell 8% to 85,000 units in 2024, still the second largest number recorded in history. 80% of all European robot installations took place in the European Union (67,800 units). Robot demand in Europe benefited from the nearshoring trend. The annual average growth rate from 2019 to 2024 was plus 3%.

**Germany**is the largest robot market in Europe and the fifth-largest in the world. Installations fell 5% to 26,982 units in 2024, which is the second-best result recorded after the record year of 2023. This represents a 32% market share of the annual total in Europe. The number of installations in **Italy**, the second largest European market, fell by 16% to 8,783 units. **Spain**is now in third place (5,100 units), with a strong demand from the automotive industry. **France**(4,900 units) moved down to fourth place, with a 24% decrease.

In the **UK**, industrial robot installations were down 35% to 2,500 units in 2024. The record number of 3,800 units in 2023 was a one-off peak, driven by the “super-deduction” tax credit program, which ended after the first quarter of 2023. Installation counts moved sideways with some cyclicity over the past decade. Robot installations in the UK rank 19th worldwide in 2024.

## The Americas

Robot installations in the Americas exceeded 50,000 units for the fourth year in a row: 50,100 units were installed in 2024, down 10% below the level reached 2023.

The **United States**, the largest regional market, accounted for 68% of installations in the Americas in 2024. Robot installations were down by 9% to 34,200 units. The United States imports most of its robots from Japan and Europe, with few domestic suppliers. However, there are numerous domestic robot system integrators implementing robotic automation solutions.

Total installations in **Mexico**reached 5,600 units in 2024, a decrease of 4%. The automotive industry remained the key customer of industrial robots in Mexico, accounting for 63% of the installations in 2024.

In **Canada**, robot installations declined by 12% to 3,800 units. Installation figures in Canada largely depend on automotive investment cycles. The share of the car industry was 47% in 2024.

## Outlook

The OECD and the IMF expect global growth in a range of 2.9% to 3.0% in 2025 and 2.9% and 3.1% in 2026. However, geopolitical tensions, violent conflicts in Eastern Europe and the Middle East, and trade disruptions are exerting their negative impact on the global economy.

The robotics industry is not immune to global macroeconomic conditions, but there is no indication that the overall long-term growth trend will come to an end any time soon. While regional trends vary substantially, the aggregate global trajectory remains positive. Globally, robot installations are expected to grow by 6% to 575,000 units in 2025. By 2028, the 700,000-unit mark will be surpassed.

args.summary:
The International Federation of Robotics (IFR) released its World Robotics 2025 report on industrial robots on September 25, 2025, in Frankfurt. The report shows 542,000 industrial robots were installed globally in 2024, more than double the number from 10 years ago and marking the fourth consecutive year of annual installations exceeding 500,000 units. This was the second highest annual installation count in history, only 2% below the all-time high from two years prior. The global operational stock of industrial robots reached 4,664,000 units in 2024, a 9% increase year-over-year.

**Regional breakdown:** Asia accounted for 74% of new deployments in 2024, followed by Europe (16%) and the Americas (9%). China remains by far the world's largest market with 295,000 installations (54% of global deployments) — the highest annual total on record. For the first time, Chinese manufacturers sold more than foreign suppliers in their home market, with domestic market share climbing to 57% (up from about 28% over the past decade). China's operational robot stock exceeded 2 million units in 2024. Japan was the second-largest market with 44,500 units (-4%), followed by the Republic of Korea with 30,600 units (-3%). India grew 7% to a record 9,100 units, ranking sixth worldwide.

**Europe:** European installations fell 8% to 85,000 units (still the second largest total on record), with the EU accounting for 80% (67,800 units). Germany was the largest European market (26,982 units, -5%, fifth largest globally), followed by Italy (8,783 units, -16%), Spain (5,100 units), France (4,900 units, -24%), and the UK (2,500 units, -35%). The UK's sharp decline was attributed to the end of the "super-deduction" tax credit program that had driven a record year in 2023.

**The Americas:** Installations exceeded 50,000 units for the fourth consecutive year at 50,100 units (-10%). The United States accounted for 68% of regional installations with 34,200 units (-9%), and imports most of its robots from Japan and Europe. Mexico installed 5,600 units (-4%) with automotive as the key customer (63% share), while Canada declined 12% to 3,800 units.

**Outlook:** The OECD and IMF expect global growth of 2.9%-3.0% in 2025 and 2.9%-3.1% in 2026, though geopolitical tensions and trade disruptions pose risks. IFR projects global robot installations to grow 6% to 575,000 units in 2025 and surpass 700,000 units by 2028. IFR President Takayuki Ito noted the transition of many industries into the digital and automated age has driven a huge surge in demand, with no indication the long-term growth trend will end. The report includes downloadable market presentations, regional press releases, and graphs for key markets including China, Germany, India, and the Americas.
args.key_excerpts: "The new World Robotics statistics show 2024 the second highest annual installation count of industrial robots in history - only 2% lower than the all-time-high two years ago," says Takayuki Ito, President of the International Federation of Robotics.
