# Top Manufacturing Tech Applications in 2025

Six experts from across the industrial automation sector weigh in with their expectations about the technologies manufacturers will use most effectively this year.

[David Greenfield](/13743059)

Jan. 14, 2025

11 min read

[Add Us On Google](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=automationworld.com)

© Andreyi Armiagov | Dreamstime.com

![Automated production cell with robot arm](https://img.automationworld.com/files/base/ebm/automationworld/image/2025/01/677d60c0048efe4d50be22e6-dreamstime_m_136542004.png?auto=format,compress&fit=fill&fill=blur&q=45?w=250&width=250)

Let me start by saying I’m not much of a fan of predictions. Especially when it comes to technology. It’s too easy for prognosticators to throw out ideas of what may or may not come to pass only to plead mea culpa when those predictions prove to be wildly off base.

On the other hand, I do appreciate insights from experts working in the field who offer, not predictions, but clear trend outlines of where things are likely headed based on what they’ve been seeing develop over the past few years.

That’s what this article captures — an array of insights from industry leaders like Ira Moskowitz, CEO of [Advanced Robotics for Manufacturing](https://arminstitute.org), an institute in the Manufacturing USA Network; Nishanth Vallabhu, strategic business unit leader for manufacturing at [Cognizant](https://www.cognizant.com/us/en); Aaron Merkin, chief technology officer at [Fluke Reliability](https://reliability.fluke.com); Simon D. Kim, CEO and founder of manufacturing software company [Glassdome](https://glassdome.com); Edwin van den Maagdenberg, vice president of industrial automation for Europe at [Honeywell](https://automation.honeywell.com/us/en); and Tim Long, global head of manufacturing at [Snowflake](https://www.snowflake.com/en/).

### Artificial intelligence outlook

It should come as no surprise that artificial intelligence (AI) is the main technology businesses of all kinds have been taking a hard look at over the past few years, particularly in 2024. With numerous companies deploying not just AI-powered data analytics, but generative AI technologies like copilots in the past year, there’s bound to be a high level of expectations for AI in 2025 (see links at the end of this article to read about applications of AI in manufacturing). Here’s what we heard from our contributors:

![Ira Moskowitz, Advanced Robotics for Manufacturing](https://img.automationworld.com/files/base/ebm/automationworld/image/2025/01/677d5a00048efe5ad2be2256-moskowitz.png?auto=format,compress&fit=max&q=45?w=250&width=250)

Ira Moskowitz, CEO of Advanced Robotics for Manufacturing

“In 2025, we’ll see more focus on the practical applications of AI in manufacturing, particularly in robotics for manufacturing,” said Advanced Robotics for Manufacturing’s Ira Moskowitz. “AI can be enabled in a manufacturing environment like never before because it can now operate in the confluence of digital twins and digital backbones that provide the modeling required for intelligent systems; it is enabled by powerful new sensors for vision and path planning; and it is powered by massive computing available in machines the size of a laptop or in the cloud, with virtually unlimited network storage.”

Fluke Reliability’s Aaron Merkin pointed to the integration of AI and predictive maintenance into supply chain planning to enable demand forecasting for spare parts in advance and with greater precision. “This facilitates a transition from just-in-case to just-in-time MRO inventory management,” he said. “The result is not only a reduction in spare parts inventory levels with the associated capital costs, but it also helps minimize unplanned downtime. With effective inventory management as a major focus, more organizations are moving from spreadsheets or pen-and-paper-based inventories to virtual storerooms that give an accurate, up-to-the-minute picture of supply levels. RFID technology and IIoT (industrial Internet of Things) devices can provide real-time parts tracking. These tools provide workers with real-time visibility into supply levels, enabling them to search for parts quickly, see what’s on hand and where it’s located, and reserve it for their tasks, all from a mobile device. This also benefits multi-site facilities, which can share spare parts and reduce the uncertainty of relying on supply chain vendors. For example, our customer, Hexpol, has been successful in streamlining their supply chain by facilitating inter-plant sharing, circumventing long lead times between plants in neighboring states and driving efficiency.”

> By harnessing real-time data insights and digital augmentation, AI can enable a two-year novice to quickly develop decision making capabilities more akin to those of a 30-year veteran. — van den Maagdeberg

![Aaron Merkin, Fluke Reliability](https://img.automationworld.com/files/base/ebm/automationworld/image/2025/01/677d59df688f7a373d4fd201-merkin.png?auto=format,compress&fit=max&q=45?w=250&width=250)

Aaron Merkin, chief technology officer at Fluke Reliability

Merkin added that he also sees AI as being critical to making recommendations for restocking schedules so that companies have a strategic edge to maintain optimal inventory levels.

“Utilizing predictive insights, companies gain the foresight needed to restock replacement parts and avoid unexpected downtime due to shipment delays. It’s all about predictability, and every day gained from increased visibility into their operations is another day of avoiding downtime,” he said. “For example, a common challenge facing our customers is how to efficiently maintain assets across the plant floor in single facilities or cross-site operations with a smaller, potentially lower-skilled workforce. Remote condition monitoring solutions powered by AI analytics coupled with wireless sensor technology enables a smaller group of technicians to maintain visibility into asset health that would have previously required a large number of distributed boots on the ground.”

Citing specific operations enhancement applications for AI, Snowflake’s Tim Long expects customized, manufacturing-specific AI solutions will outperform generic options in 2025. “These custom AI systems can be trained on manufacturing-specific data, allowing them to better understand the nuanced processes of individual organizations,” he said. “From supply chain risk assessments to predictive maintenance and design optimization, these customized AI solutions will deliver significantly higher ROI compared to one-size-fits-all approaches.”

![Tim Long, Snowflake](https://img.automationworld.com/files/base/ebm/automationworld/image/2025/01/677d5a47048efe7f62be225d-long.png?auto=format,compress&fit=max&q=45?w=250&width=250)

Tim Long, global head of manufacturing at Snowflake

Long highlighted AI-powered vision applications as being particularly key to improving manufacturing quality control processes in the near term. “These AI systems will not only aid in product quality improvement but also accelerate production by eliminating bottlenecks associated with manual inspection,” he explained. “Imagine a production line where every product is inspected in milliseconds with a high degree of accuracy and consistency. This is the not-so-distant future, freeing up production workers to focus on higher-level tasks such as root cause analysis or process improvement. Early adopters will see substantial gains in both product quality and production speed.”

### Retirements will drive an increase in manufacturing tech adoption

Though industry verticals such as automotive and aerospace have long been leaders of cutting-edge tech use in manufacturing, the industry as a whole has typically taken a more cautious approach. But the growing number of experienced industry retirees, coupled with a dearth of new hires in manufacturing, is expected to change industry’s course when it comes to new tech adoption. This change can be seen in how manufacturing tech is no longer primarily viewed as just a means of improving operations. Instead, it’s increasingly seen as a critical means of maintaining operations as the number of potential workers remains below industry’s need (Merkin’s comments above about remote condition monitoring underscore this point of view).

> A common challenge facing our customers is how to efficiently maintain assets across the plant floor in single facilities or cross-site operations with a smaller, potentially lower-skilled workforce. Remote condition monitoring solutions powered by AI analytics coupled with wireless sensor technology enables a smaller group of technicians to maintain visibility into asset health that would have previously required a large number of distributed boots on the ground.” — Merkin

![Simon D. Kim, Glassdome](https://img.automationworld.com/files/base/ebm/automationworld/image/2025/01/677d59a8d37893798bfa6e63-glassdome_ceo_and_cofounder_simon_kim.png?auto=format,compress&fit=max&q=45?w=250&width=250)

Simon D. Kim, CEO and founder of manufacturing software company Glassdome

Glassdome’s Simon D. Kim said, “An entire generation of employees who’ve been with manufacturers for decades are about to retire or have already done so. Starting in 2025, manufacturers will lean on AI, data and other technologies to replace some of this expertise and knowledge that will leave the industry.”

He expects that, in 2025, factories will “continue their digital transition as the crossover between the digital world and manufacturing continues with technologies like AI-powered drones and more robots on factory floors. As AI, automation and machine learning are becoming the norm, data will play an even greater role in the manufacturing process.”

Moskowitz points out, however, that technology alone cannot address the most significant hurdles that manufacturers face amid the current industrial workforce gap. “Not only will we see a growing emphasis on collaborative technologies in 2025, such as collaborative robots that augment workforce gaps, but we’ll also see a growing emphasis on workforce development,” he said. “We’ll see more action around engaging the next generation of manufacturers earlier in their lives. But for more immediate impact, we’ll see more manufacturers looking to upskill their workers to give them the training needed to work alongside advanced technologies. We’ll see more of an emphasis around understanding industry transferrable skills so that those who are looking to make a career change can make the shift into manufacturing more easily.”

![Edwin van den Maagdenberg, Honeywell](https://img.automationworld.com/files/base/ebm/automationworld/image/2025/01/677d59c2f78e60400d75c269-maagdenberg.png?auto=format,compress&fit=max&q=45?w=250&width=250)

Edwin van den Maagdenberg, vice president of industrial automation for Europe at Honeywell

Honeywell’s Edwin van den Maagdenberg added that he expects AI to “play a transformative role here to more quickly upskill workers and close critical skills gaps within manufacturing. By harnessing real-time data insights and digital augmentation, AI can enable a two-year novice to quickly develop decision making capabilities more akin to those of a 30-year veteran.”

To enable the fewer workers entering industry to assume the tasks once managed by a larger workforce, Cognizant’s Nishanth Vallabhu said he sees operations data taking center stage as the demand for “servitization” grows in manufacturing. He explained that, historically, “manufacturing has focused on production efficiency and quality control over customer engagement. However, as manufacturers shift toward a servitization model — offering ongoing services throughout a product’s lifecycle, rather than just selling a standalone product — they will need to analyze product use and performance data more extensively. AI will enable manufacturers to generate new revenue streams by providing additional services such as maintenance and predictive analytics to keep customers engaged long after the initial product exits the factory.”

> Historically, manufacturing has focused on production efficiency and quality control over customer engagement. However, as manufacturers shift toward a servitization model — offering ongoing services throughout a product’s lifecycle, rather than just selling a standalone product — they will need to analyze product use and performance data more extensively — Vallabhu

![Nishanth Vallabhu, Cognizant](https://img.automationworld.com/files/base/ebm/automationworld/image/2025/01/677d5a1d9bbe3b846a0a3ba4-vallabhu.png?auto=format,compress&fit=max&q=45?w=250&width=250)

Nishanth Vallabhu, strategic business unit leader for manufacturing at Cognizant

### The impact of a new U.S. government and the ongoing focus on sustainability

“The political shifts in the United States and abroad will profoundly affect manufacturing,” said Kim. “I expect more investment in the manufacturing sector in the U.S. in 2025 as the new administration works to boost manufacturing and increase the number of manufacturing jobs. Trump recently promised to fast-track permitting for companies that invest $1 billion in the U.S., and many manufacturers are undoubtedly capable of such an investment. On the flip side, the [new administration’s] emphasis on protectionism may hurt a manufacturing sector that depends on the global supply chain.”

Kim added that, even if the government rolls back climate regulations in the U.S., sustainability will remain relevant to manufacturers in 2025. “Manufacturing companies must consider sustainability to compete globally,” he explained. “Manufacturers that export to the EU or own subsidiaries there will be expected to comply with EU environmental regulations. Additionally, certain states, notably California, New York and other parts of the U.S., will also likely keep rules in place that affect the manufacturing sector.”

Merkin noted how predictive maintenance is increasingly being discussed in conversations around sustainable operations. “It optimizes equipment for reliability and environmental impact,” he said. “By enhancing renewable energy asset availability, extending equipment lifespans and lowering emissions through improved energy efficiency, predictive maintenance supports companies’ ESG (environmental, social and governance) goals. The current economic climate has amplified the focus on efficiency and maintaining equipment rather than replacing it. More businesses want to automate their operations with tactics like condition monitoring and connected reliability.”

AI will play a role in sustainability as well, according to Long, who said manufacturers will increasingly use AI in 2025 to boost efficiency and sustainability — addressing the longstanding challenges of improving shop floor productivity while reducing carbon footprints. “This transformation isn't just about being environmentally friendly, it's about staying competitive in a rapidly changing landscape,” he said. “AI-powered systems can optimize energy consumption at various levels, from individual machine operations to entire production lines. We see AI being used to analyze energy usage patterns, predicting peaks and troughs, and automatically adjusting processes to minimize waste. This ongoing shift will be driven by a combination of regulatory pressures, evolving customer expectations and heightened shareholder expectations.”

> We see AI being used to analyze energy usage patterns, predicting peaks and troughs, and automatically adjusting processes to minimize waste. This ongoing shift will be driven by a combination of regulatory pressures, evolving customer expectations, and heightened shareholder expectations. — Long

With manufacturers increasingly being held accountable for the sustainability of their entire supply chains, Vallabhu expects more manufacturers to showcase strong sustainability credentials to maintain and attract business. “Generative AI is poised to simplify and streamline this process, automating complex, data-intensive reporting methods,” he said. “It can also be used to run simulations and compare the sustainability impact of different scenarios and alternatives. In turn, manufacturers will be able to more effectively track, report and demonstrate their sustainability efforts to meet growing expectations.”

Noting the synergy between automation and energy efficiency as an area of significant opportunity for manufacturers, van den Maagdenberg expects increased use of AI-powered automation to optimize energy use across industrial processes to reduce energy intensity and operational costs. “AI-enhanced control systems allow plants and facilities to operate at peak performance for longer periods, improving efficiency while minimizing downtime,” he said. He also highlighted how automation is playing a critical role in shaping the future of the energy sector. “One example of technology that is set to benefit from AI’s enhanced automation capabilities is energy storage and grid management. Battery energy storage systems are essential for enabling renewable power. The process of storing and releasing that energy into the grid is a complex process, and automation plays a critical role in managing it effectively. As more industrial facilities develop their own microgrids, the demand for nimble, scalable automation and control systems to run these grids and integrate renewable energy sources will only grow. AI can play a valuable role in optimizing this infrastructure, ensuring efficient operation and maximum reliability.”

***Highlights of AI in manufacturing applications from Automation World:***

* **[Siemens Industrial Copilot Uses AI for Human-Machine Collaboration](https://www.automationworld.com/factory/plant-maintenance/article/33014057/siemens-industrial-copilot-uses-ai-for-human-machine-collaboration)**
* **[Rockwell Automation's AI Vision Tech for Closed-Loop Quality Control](https://www.automationworld.com/analytics/article/55251927/rockwell-automations-ai-vision-tech-for-closed-loop-quality-control)**
* **[Generative AI for Defect Detection and Root Cause Analysis](https://www.automationworld.com/analytics/article/55249343/generative-ai-fordefect-detection-and-root-cause-analysis)**
* **[Developing a Strategic Approach to Production-Enhancing AI](https://www.automationworld.com/analytics/article/55239507/developing-a-strategic-approach-to-production-enhancing-ai)**

The article highlights three major themes:
1. AI is the dominant technology trend, with applications ranging from predictive maintenance and quality control to energy optimization and workforce upskilling.
2. Workforce retirements are driving increased tech adoption, as manufacturing's aging workforce leaves the industry and fewer new workers enter, making technology critical for maintaining operations.
3. Sustainability and energy efficiency remain priorities, with predictive maintenance supporting ESG goals, and political shifts in the U.S. creating both opportunities and challenges for manufacturers.

Recommended related articles on AI in manufacturing from Automation World include Siemens Industrial Copilot for human-machine collaboration, Rockwell Automation's AI vision tech for closed-loop quality control, generative AI for defect detection, and strategic approaches to production-enhancing AI.
args.key_excerpts: "In 2025, we'll see more focus on the practical applications of AI in manufacturing, particularly in robotics for manufacturing. AI can be enabled in a manufacturing environment like never before because it can now operate in the confluence of digital twins and digital backbones that provide the modeling required for intelligent systems; it is enabled by powerful new sensors for vision and path planning; and it is powered by massive computing available in machines the size of a laptop or in the cloud, with virtually unlimited network storage." — Ira Moskowitz

Manufacturing automation has evolved far beyond the simple conveyor belts and assembly lines that once defined factory floors. What we’re witnessing now is a complete reimagining of how products get made.

We’ve reached a point where factories can now run themselves. Machines talk to each other, make decisions without human input, and even predict when they’ll need maintenance.

**But here’s what makes this era different: We’re not just replacing workers with machines. We’re creating intelligent systems that work alongside people to achieve results neither could accomplish alone.**

For manufacturing executives, this creates both significant opportunities and critical strategic decision-making. Companies across industries are implementing these technologies to reduce costs, improve quality, and respond faster to market demands. The businesses that understand and adopt these capabilities position themselves for long-term success.

This article will walk you through the key technologies driving this shift, including collaborative robots working on factory floors and AI systems that optimize entire production schedules. You’ll also discover how Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems serve as the nerve center connecting all these automated components.

## The Evolution of Manufacturing Automation [](https://www.top10erp.org/blog/the-next-era-of-manufacturing-automation-smart-factories-and-industry-4-0#the-evolution-of-manufacturing-automation "Direct link to The Evolution of Manufacturing Automation")

Manufacturing automation didn’t happen overnight. It’s been building momentum for over a century, with each wave of innovation solving problems the previous generation couldn’t. Understanding this progression helps explain why we’re at such a critical inflection point today.

### From Mechanization to Smart Factories

The journey from Henry Ford’s assembly line to today’s smart factories tells a story of continuous innovation driven by one constant: the need to do more with less.

Ford’s assembly line in the early 1900 s[cut vehicle production time from over 12 hours to just 93 minutes](https://guides.loc.gov/this-month-in-business-history/October/Ford). That breakthrough established the foundation for everything that followed. However, Ford’s system was a rigid one, which was great for producing large quantities of identical black Model T cars, but didn’t work well when customer demands changed.

The mid-20 th century introduced programmable logic controllers (PLCs), enabling machines to follow computer instructions rather than relying solely on mechanical processes. Suddenly, the same equipment could handle different tasks by simply changing the program. This flexibility opened the doors that fixed automation had kept closed.

Industrial robots arrived later in the 20 th century, bringing precision to welding, painting, and assembly work. These were purpose-built machines that could work tirelessly with accuracy humans couldn’t match.

### Industry 4.0 and Smart Factories

We’ve now entered[the era of Industry 4.0](https://www.top10erp.org/blog/digital-transformation-in-manufacturing) and smart factories. This is a fundamental shift in how we think about manufacturing.

![Image 8: Automation for manufacturing factories](blob:http://localhost/964d6c554254370ecdfc034c321756fd)

A smart factory is an interconnected ecosystem where machines, sensors, and software communicate in real-time to make autonomous decisions. These facilities[adjust production schedules in response to supply chain disruptions](https://www.top10erp.org/blog/erp-supply-chain), predict equipment failures before they occur, and customize products without interrupting the production line.

While previous automation focused on speed and consistency, today’s systems add learning and adaptation. The difference is intelligence.

### Key Drivers Behind Automation Growth

Three significant forces are driving manufacturers toward automation at a faster pace than ever before:

**Rising Labor Costs and Shortages**: [Skilled workers are retiring faster](https://www.top10erp.org/blog/silver-tsunami) than companies can replace them, driving up costs while making it harder to maintain consistent production.

**Global Competition**: Companies must compete with facilities worldwide. Automation levels the playing field by enabling highly efficient production that can compete with lower overseas labor costs.

**Supply Chain Resilience**: Recent global disruptions highlighted[supply chain vulnerabilities](https://www.top10erp.org/whitepaper-library/the-supply-chain-of-the-future-2). Automation enables reshoring, bringing production closer to customers.

## Robotics in Manufacturing [](https://www.top10erp.org/blog/the-next-era-of-manufacturing-automation-smart-factories-and-industry-4-0#robotics-in-manufacturing "Direct link to Robotics in Manufacturing")

[Modern manufacturing robotics](https://www.top10erp.org/blog/robotics-in-manufacturing) goes far beyond the isolated robotic arms that defined the previous decades. While traditional industrial robots excel at repetitive, high-precision tasks like welding, painting, and assembly, the next level of innovation comes from collaborative robots, also known as ​“cobots.”

Unlike traditional robots operating in safety cages, cobots work safely alongside people. They handle heavy lifting and precision work while human workers focus on problem-solving and complex assembly tasks.

### Benefits of Robotics in Manufacturing

*   **Precision and Consistency**: Robots perform identical motions with perfect precision, eliminating the variability that creates defects.
*   **Increased Throughput**: Continuous operation without fatigue or shift changes provides predictable cycle times.
*   **Enhanced Worker Safety**: Robots excel in hazardous environments, allowing human workers to focus on safer, more engaging tasks.

## Artificial Intelligence: The Brain Behind Smart Factories [](https://www.top10erp.org/blog/the-next-era-of-manufacturing-automation-smart-factories-and-industry-4-0#artificial-intelligence-the-brain-behind-smart-factories "Direct link to Artificial Intelligence: The Brain Behind Smart Factories")

If robots are the muscles of modern manufacturing, artificial intelligence is the brain.[AI turns factory data into actionable insights](https://www.top10erp.org/blog/ai-in-erp), enabling machines to learn, predict, and make decisions without constant human oversight.

### AI-Driven Decision-Making

AI systems analyze real-time sensor data from temperature, vibration, and speed monitors to predict equipment failures before they happen. [This predictive maintenance approach](https://www.top10erp.org/whitepaper-library/ai-in-the-manufacturing-industry) eliminates both costly unexpected breakdowns and unnecessary scheduled maintenance.

[AI-powered vision systems](https://www.top10erp.org/blog/how-is-ai-reshaping-manufacturing-in-2026)also inspect products at full production speed, detecting defects that human inspectors might miss while learning quality standards from thousands of product examples.

### Autonomous Manufacturing Systems

These advanced systems go beyond monitoring to actively manage production without human intervention. They[analyze data across the entire factory floor](https://www.top10erp.org/blog/erp-analytics) and automatically implement changes by adjusting machine speeds to reduce defects, modifying operation sequences to improve throughput, or rerouting production when equipment issues arise. The systems measure results and continuously refine processes, creating truly self-optimizing production lines.

## Key Technologies Driving Factory Automation [](https://www.top10erp.org/blog/the-next-era-of-manufacturing-automation-smart-factories-and-industry-4-0#key-technologies-driving-factory-automation "Direct link to Key Technologies Driving Factory Automation")

Beyond robots and AI, several other technologies are shaping how manufacturers operate their factories today. These systems work together to create the connected, intelligent factories that define manufacturing automation.

**Some leading technologies in use today include**

*   **Smart Sensors** monitor equipment health through temperature, vibration, and pressure readings. These sensors detect developing mechanical problems before they cause breakdowns, enabling the implementation of predictive maintenance strategies.
*   **Industrial IoT Devices** collect real-time data on machine performance, environmental conditions, and material usage. This constant data stream feeds AI systems, providing visibility into every aspect of factory operations.
*   **3 D Printing** enables rapid prototyping and the production of custom tooling. Manufacturers use 3 D printing to create jigs, fixtures, and low-volume custom parts without the tooling costs associated with traditional manufacturing methods.
*   **Digital Twins** are virtual replicas of physical systems that update in real-time using sensor data. Engineers can test changes and simulate different scenarios in the digital environment before implementing them on the actual production line.

Looking ahead, ​“lights-out” manufacturing will enable fully automated facilities that run production without human oversight for extended periods. And,[digital twins will model entire factories](https://www.top10erp.org/blog/digital-twin-manufacturing-guide), enabling manufacturers to test major changes in risk-free virtual environments.

### Industry 5.0 is Emerging at the Next Phase

Industry 5.0 emphasizes human-machine collaboration where automation augments rather than replaces human creativity and decision-making. This approach prioritizes sustainability and social responsibility by using automation to achieve environmental goals while creating more meaningful and safer work for employees.

For example, Industry 5.0 systems use AI to optimize energy consumption by scheduling production during off-peak hours when renewable energy is most available. And companies are redesigning workflows so automation handles physically demanding or hazardous tasks so employees can focus on skilled work that offers better career development opportunities and higher job satisfaction.

“We’re entering a phase where robotics will move far beyond structured factory floors. We’ll see a shift from rigid, pre-programmed systems to intelligent, reconfigurable machines that can operate in dynamic environments, whether that’s a warehouse, a farm, a hospital, a home, or even a disaster zone.” –Daniela Rus, Director, Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory (CSAIL), MIT (2025) Capgem​i​ni​.com 

## Industries Leading Automation Innovation [](https://www.top10erp.org/blog/the-next-era-of-manufacturing-automation-smart-factories-and-industry-4-0#industries-leading-automation-innovation "Direct link to Industries Leading Automation Innovation")

Manufacturing sectors adopt automation technologies at varying paces, dependent upon their unique requirements and competitive pressures. Understanding how automation applies across industries can help manufacturers identify relevant opportunities for their own operations.

![Image 9: Manufacturing automation industries](blob:http://localhost/34ea28bd91675cba3cb38931c41fc120)

### Automotive

The[automotive industry continues to push the boundaries of automation](https://www.top10erp.org/blog/finding-the-right-erp-for-your-automotive-operation-what-to-know-before-you-buy), particularly in electric vehicle manufacturing. Robots handle welding, painting, and assembly with precision surpassing manual processes, while automated systems perform high-voltage testing and handle hazardous materials.

### Electronics &High Tech

Electronics manufacturing demands precision that only automated systems can achieve consistently. Pick-and-place machines position components smaller than rice grains with thousandth-of-an-inch accuracy, while test equipment performs thousands of electrical checks in seconds.

### Food &Beverage

Food and Beverage manufacturers use automation to ensure consistency and safety while handling delicate products at high speeds. Robotic systems handle products without damage while ensuring accurate labeling, and[ERP integration tracks every ingredient](https://www.top10erp.org/blog/the-history-of-food-and-beverage-manufacturing)for rapid quality issue response.

### Medical Devices

Medical device production demands extreme precision and traceability while meeting strict regulatory requirements. Automated systems handle microscopic components and delicate materials required for implants, surgical instruments, and diagnostic devices.

### Small &Mid-Sized Manufacturers

Automation technology, which once required massive investments, is becoming increasingly accessible to smaller manufacturers. Cobots cost significantly less than traditional robots,[cloud-based ERP eliminates expensive servers](https://www.top10erp.org/blog/9-reasons-why-your-business-should-switch-to-cloud-based-erp-system), and smaller companies can now compete on efficiency rather than price alone.

## Current Trends and Challenges in Manufacturing Automation [](https://www.top10erp.org/blog/the-next-era-of-manufacturing-automation-smart-factories-and-industry-4-0#current-trends-and-challenges-in-manufacturing-automation "Direct link to Current Trends and Challenges in Manufacturing Automation")

Manufacturing automation continues to evolve rapidly; however, successful implementation requires an understanding of both the opportunities and obstacles associated with these advanced systems.

### Key Trends Shaping the Manufacturing Sector Today

**Shift Toward Smart Factories and Industry 4.0**

Manufacturers are moving beyond isolated automated systems toward fully integrated smart factories that connect every machine, sensor, and process into a unified network. This enables the production of personalized products at scale with the cost efficiency of traditional manufacturing.

**Cloud ERP and Connected Automation**

Cloud-based ERP systems offer lower upfront costs and the ability to connect with automation equipment from anywhere. This connectivity supports remote monitoring and predictive analytics across multiple facilities.

**Edge Computing and Real-Time Processing**

Manufacturers are moving computing power closer to the factory floor rather than relying on cloud-based processing for some time-critical decisions. Edge computing enables millisecond response times for safety systems and quality control, eliminating the need for internet connectivity.

**Generative AI for Manufacturing Operations**

Beyond predictive maintenance,[generative AI is creating ​“virtual coworkers” that analyze production data](https://www.top10erp.org/erp-software-comparison/by-vendor/infor-solutions)and generate reports automatically. These systems can plan complex workflows and optimize shift handovers by sorting relevant from irrelevant information.

**Augmented Reality (AR) for Maintenance and Training**

AR technology enables remote equipment servicing and immersive training programs. Technicians receive step-by-step repair instructions overlaid on real equipment, while new employees practice on virtual systems before working with actual machinery.

**Modular and Flexible Manufacturing Systems**

Instead of fixed production lines, manufacturers are adopting modular systems that can be quickly reconfigured for different products. This trend supports mass customization and shorter product lifecycles.

**Sustainability Through Energy-Efficient Automation**

Automated systems optimize energy usage and reduce material waste by adjusting operations based on demand and maintaining optimal conditions. Smart manufacturing systems track resource consumption in real-time, helping manufacturers meet sustainability goals while reducing costs.

### Implementation Challenges

*   **High Initial Investment**: Manufacturing automation requires significant upfront investment in equipment, software, integration, and training. Implementation costs extend beyond equipment purchases to include planning and ongoing maintenance requirements.
*   **Workforce Transition**: Automation changes job requirements, often eliminating some positions while creating new ones. Companies must invest in training programs to help employees transition and develop internal expertise for operating and maintaining automated systems.
*   **Cybersecurity Risks**: Connected systems create new security vulnerabilities that can disrupt production or compromise information if not properly addressed. Manufacturers must implement comprehensive cybersecurity strategies, including access controls, network segmentation, and regular security updates.

ERP as the Backbone of Manufacturing Automation

Since it’s our focus, we would be remiss if we didn’t address the role of ERP and Automation in Manufacturing. While automation technologies generate tremendous value individually, their real power emerges when they work together as a unified system.[ERP manufacturing software](https://www.top10erp.org/blog/manufacturing-erp) serves as the unifier connecting robots, AI, sensors, and production equipment. You really can’t have successful automation without it.

### How ERP Optimizes Automation

ERP systems serve as the central hub for automated manufacturing, collecting data from every robotic cell, sensor, and machine on the factory floor and sharing it across departments in real-time. For example, when a robotic assembly cell completes a batch, the ERP system[automatically updates inventory levels](https://www.top10erp.org/blog/7_ways_inventory_tracking_has_changed_in_modern_warehousing), triggers the next production step, and adjusts schedules based on actual performance rather than estimates.

The system manages complex interactions between production schedules, material availability, and machine capacity without manual intervention. When orders change or deliveries face delays, the ERP system automatically reallocates resources. It then adjusts timelines, ensuring automated systems always have the right materials and instructions to maintain optimal production flow.

### ERP Integration Benefits

ERP dashboards display real-time information about automated processes in formats managers can easily and quickly understand. Production supervisors see which robotic cells run efficiently, quality managers track defect rates from AI systems, and maintenance teams view equipment health data from IoT sensors.

It was updated as of Sep 29, 2025 (with a listing of Jul 10, 2026). The article explores how manufacturing automation has evolved from simple assembly lines to intelligent, self-optimizing smart factories, and examines the technologies, industries, trends, and challenges shaping this transformation.

**Key sections and content:**

1. **Evolution of Manufacturing Automation**: Traces the progression from Henry Ford's assembly line (which cut vehicle production time from over 12 hours to just 93 minutes) to programmable logic controllers (PLCs), industrial robots, and now Industry 4.0 smart factories. Smart factories are described as interconnected ecosystems where machines, sensors, and software communicate in real-time to make autonomous decisions.

2. **Key Drivers Behind Automation Growth**: Three main forces are pushing manufacturers toward automation: (1) rising labor costs and shortages (skilled workers retiring faster than they can be replaced), (2) global competition (automation levels the playing field against lower overseas labor costs), and (3) supply chain resilience (automation enables reshoring).

3. **Robotics**: Collaborative robots ("cobots") work safely alongside people, unlike traditional robots in safety cages. Benefits include precision/consistency, increased throughput, and enhanced worker safety.

4. **AI as the Brain of Smart Factories**: AI analyzes real-time sensor data for predictive maintenance, uses machine vision to detect product defects, and enables autonomous manufacturing systems that adjust machine speeds, modify operation sequences, and reroute production without human intervention.

5. **Key Technologies**: Smart sensors, Industrial IoT devices, 3D printing, and Digital Twins (virtual replicas updating in real-time). Future developments include "lights-out" manufacturing (fully automated facilities) and Industry 5.0, which emphasizes human-machine collaboration, sustainability, and social responsibility.

6. **Industries Leading Innovation**: Automotive (EV manufacturing), Electronics & High Tech (precise pick-and-place machines), Food & Beverage (consistency and safety), Medical Devices (precision and traceability), and Small & Mid-Sized Manufacturers (automation now more accessible via cheaper cobots and cloud-based ERP).

7. **Current Trends**: Smart factory integration, cloud ERP and connected automation, edge computing for real-time processing, generative AI "virtual coworkers," augmented reality for maintenance/training, modular flexible manufacturing systems, and sustainability through energy-efficient automation.

8. **Implementation Challenges**: High initial investment, workforce transition needs, and cybersecurity risks.

9. **ERP as the Backbone**: ERP systems serve as the central hub connecting robots, AI, sensors, and production equipment. They automatically update inventory levels, trigger production steps, adjust schedules, and provide real-time dashboards across departments.

**Notable expert quote**: Daniela Rus, Director of CSAIL at MIT (2025): "We're entering a phase where robotics will move far beyond structured factory floors. We'll see a shift from rigid, pre-programmed systems to intelligent, reconfigurable machines that can operate in dynamic environments, whether that's a warehouse, a farm, a hospital, a home, or even a disaster zone."

The page also includes extensive navigation for Top10ERP.org featuring ERP system comparisons by vendor (54+ vendors from abas ERP to Wherefour), by industry (28+ industries), by manufacturing mode, by company size, and by technology — along with links to related content such as case studies, white papers, an advisory board, and an ERP blog.

中国商飞：数字化转型智能制造之路

译名：

COMAC\'s Digital Transformation and Intelligent Manufacturing

中文关键词：

数字化转型；智能制造；中国商飞；供应链管理；大数据治理

英文关键词：

-

中文摘要：

随着5G、大数据、物联网等信息技术的快速发展与应用，现代工业制造也迎来了全新的历史机遇，许多企业纷纷开启数字化转型之路，寻求在日趋激烈的市场竞争中获得持续性竞争优势。本案例对中国商飞上航公司决策管理者面临的问题：如何实现中国商飞上航公司的数字化转型智能制造之路及创新驱动发展？重点介绍了中国商飞上航公司的数字化转型实施路线，即根据“用数据定义产品，用数据驱动制造，用数据创造价值”的发展思路，结合最新一代信息通信技术，在飞机制造的边缘层、平台层和应用层分别实现数字化、网络化、智能化，从而完成飞机制造过程的数字化转型。本案例旨在将向准备或正在推进数字化转型的企业介绍数字化转型的先进实践，同时引导学员思考不同行业、不同企业在数字化转型过程中所面临的转型动机、竞争优势获取、供应链管理变革、大数据治理等需要解决的痛点问题进行思考。

英文摘要：

With the continuous development and application of information technologies such as 5G, big data, and Internet of Things, modern industrial manufacturing has ushered in new opportunities, and companies are exploring digital transformation to obtain a sustained competitive advantage in the increasingly competitive market. As the ‘crown’ of industrial manufacturing, the development and production of aircraft are closely related to the national security and international status of a nation, and therefore have always faced considerably brutal competition. Thus, digital transformation is urgently required to improve manufacturing efficiency. This case study systematically and comprehensively introduced a smart manufacturing system and highlighted the digital transformation implementation route of Commercial Aircraft Corporation of China. This implementation route is based on the guideline of ‘defining products, driving manufacturing, and creating value with data’ , combined with the latest generation of information and communication technology, and realises the digitalisation, networking, and intelligence in edge, platform, and application layers; therefore, the digital transformation of aircraft manufacturing is completed. This case study aimed to introduce the advance practices of digital transformation to enterprises that are preparing or undergoing digital transformation, to guide students solve the challenges and difficulties that different industries and enterprises face during digital transformation, and thus to promote the overall digital transformation of China’s manufacturing industry.

**Case Details:**
- **Case Number:** CN_2020ZLGL_7856
- **Views:** 5,878
- **Authors:** 姚建明, 李民, 吴阳, 王墨竹 (from Renmin University of China Business School)
- **Enterprise:** 中国商用飞机有限责任公司 (Commercial Aircraft Corporation of China, COMAC)
- **Industry:** Transportation/Logistics
- **Discipline areas:** Digital transformation, strategic management, operations management, information systems and e-commerce, others
- **Scale:** Large enterprise
- **Language:** Chinese (with English translation)
- **Case type:** Descriptive
- **Chinese keywords:** 数字化转型 (digital transformation), 智能制造 (intelligent manufacturing), 中国商飞 (COMAC), 供应链管理 (supply chain management), 大数据治理 (big data governance)
- **Target audience:** Undergraduate, MBA, EMBA, EE programs
- **Writing method:** 采编 (field compilation)
- **Development year:** 2020

**Case Summary (Chinese):** With rapid development of 5G, big data, IoT and other information technologies, modern industrial manufacturing faces new opportunities, and many enterprises are pursuing digital transformation for sustained competitive advantage. The case focuses on the COMAC's Shanghai Aviation (上航公司) subsidiary and its digital transformation implementation route, based on the guideline of "用数据定义产品，用数据驱动制造，用数据创造价值" (define products with data, drive manufacturing with data, create value with data). Using the latest information and communication technologies, the company achieved digitalization, networking, and intelligence across the edge, platform, and application layers of aircraft manufacturing. The case aims to introduce advanced digital transformation practices to enterprises preparing for or undergoing transformation and to guide students in thinking about challenges such as transformation motivation, competitive advantage acquisition, supply chain management reform, and big data governance.

**Case Summary (English):** The case systematically introduces a smart manufacturing system and the digital transformation implementation route of COMAC, based on the guideline of 'defining products, driving manufacturing, and creating value with data', combined with the latest generation of ICT, realizing digitalisation, networking, and intelligence in edge, platform, and application layers.

**Website Navigation:** The page also provides access to the center's announcements, news, case library (including newest and popular cases), micro-cases, English cases, teaching recommendations, case submission guidelines (format standards, review criteria, submission process), and information about the China Enterprise Management Case Forum (中国企业管理案例论坛), co-hosted by Renmin University Business School and the journal 《管理世界》 since 2007.

# 中国商飞：党建铸魂领航向 科技兴翼谱新篇

时间：2024年10月14日   来源：《国企》杂志

视力保护色：




【字号 [大](javascript:void();) [中](javascript:void();) [小](javascript:void();)】

《国企》杂志2024年10月第19期封面新鲜出炉。本期封面由中国商用飞机有限责任公司党委署名。

全文如下：

**中国商飞：党建铸魂领航向 科技兴翼谱新篇**

文/中国商用飞机有限责任公司党委

   发展大型客机是建设创新型国家、提高我国自主创新能力和增强国家核心竞争力的重大战略举措。党的十八大以来，党中央高度重视科技创新，亲切关怀大飞机事业。习近平总书记亲自为大飞机事业掌舵领航，就大飞机事业做出了一系列重要指示批示，特别是2014年5月23日亲临中国商用飞机有限责任公司（简称中国商飞，英文缩写COMAC）设计研发中心视察并发表重要讲话，2022年9月30日亲切会见C919项目团队代表并参观项目展览，深刻阐述了“为什么要办好大飞机事业、怎样办好大飞机事业”等一系列全局性、根本性、战略性的重大问题，并围绕大飞机科技创新做出了重要部署。这为大飞机事业指明了方向，为推动大飞机科技创新提供了根本遵循和强大动力。

2024年是习近平总书记视察中国商飞十周年。十年来，中国商飞党委牢记“让中国的大飞机翱翔蓝天”这一崇高使命，认真学习贯彻习近平总书记重要指示批示精神，坚持党建铸魂、科技赋能，充分发挥党建工作对科技创新的引领保障作用，团结带领党员干部职工勇担重任、攻坚克难，走过了大飞机设计、制造、试验、试飞、取证、交付、运营的全过程，实现了我国大飞机从无到有的历史性跨越。“大飞机制造等取得重大成果”写入了党的二十大报告，“国产大飞机实现商飞”成为创新驱动引领高质量发展取得新成效的标志性成果。

![](./W020241014793602468785.jpg)

**抓实党的政治建设**

**筑牢大飞机高质量发展的政治基础**

习近平总书记在视察中国商飞时强调，搞大飞机和“两个一百年”目标、实现中国梦的目标是一致的，我们这样一个大国一定要有自己的大飞机，一定要把大飞机搞上去。中国商飞党委以时不我待、只争朝夕的紧迫感，始终把发展大飞机事业放到实现“两个一百年”奋斗目标、实现中华民族伟大复兴中国梦的大局中去推进，把管党治党贯穿到大飞机事业全过程，坚决扛起大飞机事业责任、全面从严治党主体责任。

C919是全球最新一代的单通道干线喷气客机。它采用先进气动设计、先进推进系统设计和先进材料，碳排放更低、燃油效率更高，对环境更加友好，客舱具有较低的噪声水平，最大载客量可达192人。中国商飞和参研参试参审单位的广大党员干部职工团结一心，奋勇推动大飞机科技创新取得突破性进展。2015年C919“总装下线”，2017年“飞上蓝天”。2022年9月29日，在经历5年多的取证之旅，完成579个试飞项目1669项试验后，C919获得中国民航局型号合格证。2023年5月28日，C919开启国内商业首航，从上海虹桥飞抵北京首都国际机场，实现中华民族百年大飞机梦。截至2024年9月，C919已安全载客超50万人次，迈入多用户、多机队运营新阶段。中国商飞成立16年来，围绕研制C919攻克了100多项重大技术难关。目前，科研人员仍在进行新的攻关。同时，中国第一款远程宽体客机C929已经确定总体技术方案，正在稳步开展研制工作。

2024年，中国商飞党委1号文件从坚持思想引领、加强组织领导、建强战斗堡垒、激励约束并重等方面，明确18条具体举措，引导党员干部职工知难而进、迎难而上、稳中求进、以进促稳的工作基调，克服难、确保稳、实现进，坚定为2024年中心工作保驾护航。中国商飞成立100个党员示范岗、50支党员攻关队，并首次创建科学家小屋建设、过冷大水滴（SLD）引导性结冰风洞设计等18支跨单位的党员联合攻关队，党员骨干奋勇争先，带头在一线破解科研项目难题。中国商飞运用党委贺信、捷报栏、嘉奖令等措施，在大飞机设计、制造、试飞等最前沿加强员工引导激励，引领保障型号任务高质量完成。

商飞智能是中国商飞2023年孵化出的一家新型工业互联网公司。这是中国商飞贯彻落实党中央要求，抢抓信息技术革命历史机遇，加快形成大飞机新质生产力的重要举措。同年，中国商飞又携手业界伙伴联合成立了商飞时代，力争抓住新能源技术在商用航空领域的发展机遇，成为全球新能源航空客户的优质供应商。成立之日起，两家创新型企业高度重视并同步建立了党组织体系，将党建工作深度融入企业发展的血脉之中，通过创新党建工作模式、强化政治引领，确保企业在信息技术与能源技术两场革命的风口浪尖上，方向明确、步伐坚定。两家企业抢抓信息技术、能源技术两场革命机遇，大力推进开放创新、跨界创新，积极塑造大飞机非对称竞争优势，加速构建大飞机产业新生态，推进大飞机智能化、网联化、绿色化发展，不断开创大飞机事业发展新局面。

把党建工作覆盖到关键技术攻关产业链。中国商飞党委探索开展大飞机产业链党建，制定《中国商飞产业链党建工作指引（试行）》，组织中国商飞所属不同层级的党组织与产业链上下游企业、高校科研院所党组织广泛深入开展党建工作，围绕打造完整而有韧性的大飞机现代产业链，积极调动资源力量加快联合攻关，开展联合学习研讨、联合创先争优、联合宣传教育、联合表彰奖励、联合服务保障、联合廉洁合规，增强各方面推进国产大飞机事业的荣誉感和凝聚力，携手产业链上下游打造“红色引擎”。

中国商飞研究出台了《关于促进中国商飞大飞机创新试验区高质量发展的若干指导意见》，推动制定了大飞机预先研究三年滚动计划并发布指南（第一批)，聚合国内外合作伙伴开展协同创新，瞄准重点难点问题进行集智攻关。围绕科技自立自强，中国商飞与上海市共建大飞机创新谷、大飞机产业园，积极发挥产业龙头作用和科技领军企业作用。围绕央地融合，积极参与浦东世博、四川成都等区域化党建工作。围绕融入民航，中国商飞与中国民航局开展“五个融合”专项行动，与中国东方航空公司（简称东航）、中国国际航空公司（简称国航）和中国南方航空公司（简称南航）共建飞机竞争力创新中心，携手建立“国产民机运营青年联盟”。

2022年，中国商飞开始筹划可持续航空燃料（SAF）在国产商用飞机上的应用。ARJ21项目团队推进系统临时党支部与中国石化石油科学研究院第十九研究室党支部等基层党组织，将党建工作与生产经营深度融合，组织党员骨干深入研究国内外SAF技术标准、试验试飞方法，围绕SAF验证应用难题开展研讨和攻关，收到了良好成效。2024年6月5日，一架ARJ21和一架C919顺利完成了首次加注SAF的演示飞行，展现了国产商用飞机良好的飞行性能。国产商用飞机的演示飞行所使用的SAF采用中国石化自主研发生物航煤生产技术，原料来自餐余废油。餐余废油经回收处理后在中国石化镇海炼化建成的国内首套生物航煤工业装置进行加工，产出生物航煤，实现了绿色资源化利用，可大幅降低碳排放。

2014年，习近平总书记在视察中国商飞设计研发中心时强调指出，“我寄希望于、寄厚望于我们这支队伍”“一定要有这个雄心壮志，一定要相信我们是会实现这样一个伟大目标的”。2022年，习近平总书记在会见C919项目团队代表时对大家表示：“你们是国家栋梁、英雄功臣……”习近平总书记的话语，不仅是对团队的鞭策，而且是对中国航空梦的有力鼓舞，激发着每一位航空人内心深处的自豪感与使命感。

人才是大飞机事业的中流砥柱。中国商飞党委深刻认识商用飞机人才稀缺性、竞争性、全球性、成长周期长的特点，始终把人才作为“第一资源”，在科技人才队伍建设上倾注心血，加强各类人才队伍特别是科技人才队伍建设，为推进大飞机科技创新提供人力资源和智力资源基础。

实施“万人精兵工程”，推进科技人才培养。中国商飞党委加快培育战略人才力量，贯通实施中国商飞“万人精兵工程”，在纵向分类建设“技术、技能、项目、管理”和“海外人才、急需紧缺”的“4+2”支核心队伍的基础上，横向分层建设“战略科学家、科技领军人才和创新团队、青年科技人才”和“卓越工程师”的“3+1”支科技创新主力军，制定《中国商飞党委关于贯彻落实全国组织工作会议精神的任务分解方案》《“青年拔尖计划”实施办法》等，细化制定方案，加快培育支持一批顶尖科技人才、科研骨干人才、青年科技人才。中国商飞人才总量从组建时的3000多人增加到1.7万余人，技术人才超过8000人，形成以院士、型号总师为代表的科技领军人才，以专业总师、大国工匠为代表的卓越工程师和高技能人才，以C919等项目团队、各攻关团队为代表的创新团队，锤炼了一支打不垮、打不散、知难而进、迎难而上、忠诚于大飞机事业的铁杆核心队伍。

C919项目团队被评为第一届中央企业优秀创新团队，C919控制律团队获评“央企楷模”，“大国工匠”胡双钱先进事迹被上海市委宣传部选为“感动上海”故事并进行巡回宣讲。2024年1月，“国家工程师奖”首次进行评选表彰，中国商飞工程总师、ARJ21系列总设计师陈勇被授予“国家卓越工程师”称号。

顶层统筹布局，推进大飞机产学研融通创新。中国商飞党委一体推进教育发展、科技创新、人才培养，从顶层统筹布局围绕大飞机事业实际需求和需要重点提升的技术领域，突出重点合作领域、聚焦关键问题，结合高校学科优势，设立大飞机研究院。

目前，中国商飞与上海交通大学、北京航空航天大学、南京航空航天大学、重庆大学、同济大学、西北工业大学分别建立6个大飞机研究院，与上海交通大学、西北工业大学等高校共建大飞机产教融合联盟，围绕教育优先发展、科技自立自强、人才引领驱动等领域加强合作，有组织、有体系、有侧重开展科研。中国商飞初步形成大飞机“政产学研用”相融合的技术创新体系，打造科学家小屋、创新生态大会等创新品牌，建成1个国家工程技术研究中心、1个国家重点实验室、1个院士工作站、9个省市级科创平台。深化大飞机“进校园”，持续开展“国产商用飞机校园巡展”活动。

集聚全球资源，推进科技创新国际交流合作。中国商飞党委深入践行国际科技合作倡议，坚持开放合作，举办七届COMAC国际科技创新周，推动全球科技资源、工业资源和智力资源集聚，“交流基础科学、探索前沿科技、解决疑难问题、促进创新合作”的合作机制持续迸发活力。

2024年8月17日至23日，中国商飞以“绿色·智能大飞机的新机遇”为主题，邀请来自欧洲、亚太、中东等地区59所境内外高校，以及13家科研机构和企业的近500名专家、学者积极参与，推动共同凝练科学与技术问题、联合开展科研攻关、协同培养科技人才，贯通从科学到技术到工程的创新链，推动形成更多开放创新、原始创新的丰硕成果。

增强思想引领力

滋养大飞机科技创新活力竞相迸发

习近平总书记高度重视创新文化的培育，在党的十九大报告和二十大报告中多次强调“创新文化”。今年6月，习近平总书记在全国科技大会上强调：“坚持培育创新文化，传承中华优秀传统文化的创新基因，营造鼓励探索、宽容失败的良好环境，使崇尚科学、追求创新在全社会蔚然成风。”这一重要论述充分表明，把我国建设成为科技强国，坚持培育创新文化是一项基础性工作。中国商飞大力弘扬科学家精神、劳模精神、工匠精神，在大飞机研制火热一线加强创新文化、廉洁文化建设，汇聚起同心协力攻难关、解难题、破难局的磅礴力量。

传承创新基因，培育大飞机创业精神。大飞机研制具有长期性、艰巨性、复杂性，长期不懈的努力需要强大的精神凝聚力。中国商飞党委大力培育弘扬“航空强国、四个长期、永不放弃”的大飞机创业精神：“航空强国”是大飞机人的价值导向，引领着每一位航空人向着更高更远的目标迈进；“四个长期”即长期奋斗、长期攻关、长期吃苦、长期奉献，是大飞机人的基本要求和行为准则；“永不放弃”是大飞机人的精神底色，激励着他们在挑战与困难面前坚持不懈，勇往直前。通过一系列举措，中国商飞不仅构建了坚实的精神支柱，还营造了浓厚的创新文化氛围。

推动大飞机事业蓬勃发展的征途中，离不开每一代大飞机人的不懈奋斗与创新精神。为了传承这些宝贵的精神财富，中国商飞立足大飞机人奋斗历程，精心打造了“运十”飞机、“永不放弃”雕塑、“最美奋斗者”马凤山铜像和“梦想之翼”雕塑等精神传承阵地。它们以艺术化的语言，讲述着那些关于勇气、智慧与坚持的奋斗故事，激励着后来者继续前行。其中，“运十”飞机入选国家工业遗产、2023年科学家精神教育基地，成为独特文化标识和精神教育“活课堂”。

2024年9月10日，国航首架国产大飞机C919“身披”五星红旗，正式投入运营。在国航C919商业首航活动现场，特别策划了一场意义非凡的致敬仪式——邀请了“两航”起义亲历者、国航原飞行总队长以及中国民航第一代乘务员等老一辈民航先驱亲临现场，与年轻一代共同见证了这一历史性的飞跃。这些前辈们的到来，不仅为活动增添了几分历史的厚重感，而且是对新中国航空事业从无到有、从小到大、从弱到强艰辛历程的深情回望。这份跨越时空的传承与接力，正是大飞机创业精神——航空强国、四个长期、永不放弃的生动实践之源。

为了进一步激发大飞机人的创新活力与奋斗精神，中国商飞十分重视一线先进典型宣传，用主旋律正能量凝聚攻坚奋进力量。通过在基层党组织中开展创新大赛、专业技能竞赛，在大赛中选拔技术榜样，选树大飞机奋斗者、最美商飞人等先进典型，开设《攀登路上》等宣传专栏的方式，激励大飞机人爱国奉献、矢志创新。这些活动大大提升了团队的凝聚力和战斗力。

健全各项机制，厚植创新文化土壤。中国商飞党委持续健全科技创新激励保障机制，鼓励青年科研人员创新创业，支持建设青创空间、“追风”工作室、梦幻工作室等科技创新舞台，举办四届5G工业创新成果发布会，集中发布创新成果，充分展现创新风采。同时，力戒形式主义、官僚主义，为基层减负。中国商飞认真落实《整治形式主义为基层减负若干规定》，推崇“短实新”的文风，提倡少开会、开短会，严控参会人员范围，努力让科研人员从文山会海中解脱出来，有更多精力搞科研、抓落实。加强科研诚信和作风学风建设，严格落实“三个区分开来”，营造鼓励探索、宽容失败的良好环境，推动形成风清气正的科研生态。此外，中国商飞党委全方位做好科技人才服务保障。每年确定一批实事项目，着力解决员工住房难、子女入托入园难、就医难、落户难等难题，常态化开展高层次人才专窗服务，让科技人才心无旁骛、潜心钻研，持续营造尊重劳动、尊重知识、尊重人才、尊重创造的良好氛围。

强化教育监督，塑造大飞机廉洁文化。中国商飞党委持续深入学习贯彻习近平总书记关于全面加强党的纪律建设的重要论述，抓好《关于推进党纪学习教育常态化长效化的意见》落实，巩固党纪学习教育成果，将学纪知纪明纪守纪融入日常、抓在经常，常态化推进。各级党组织教育引领党员干部时时以《中国共产党纪律处分条例》为标尺，从严从实检身正己，提升自我约束能力，筑牢防腐拒变的思想防线。同时，中国商飞党委持续释放全面从严治党越往后越严的强烈信号，促进纪检监察、巡视巡察、“三防一审”等监督贯通融合，一体推进“不敢腐、不能腐、不想腐”。特别是抓好科研领域廉洁风险防控，聚焦科研、外协、采购等领域加强重点监督，围绕“技术权力腐败防治”等开展专题调研，梳理排查“靠企吃企”廉洁风险，推动制定针对性举措，制定《深化运用“四种形态”八项规范》等制度，出台与大飞机研发合作供应商往来“七项禁令”，推动与供应商建立亲而有度、清而有为的合作关系。

为了强化廉洁文化教育，中国商飞党委编发《翱翔之道——员工廉洁文化学习手册》，制播警示教育片《迟来的忏悔》，编印警示教育材料，以案为鉴、以案促改，全面提升全体员工的廉洁自律意识，共同塑造“廉洁商飞”的鲜明形象，为大飞机事业的蓬勃发展保驾护航。

奋进强国路，启航新征程。党的二十届三中全会为中国商飞的发展再次点亮新航标，绘制了新蓝图。中国商飞深知，大飞机产业化进程的每一步都标志着国家科技实力与工业制造能力的飞跃，使命光荣、任重道远。中国商飞党委将更加紧密地团结在以习近平同志为核心的党中央周围，将党的二十届三中全会的精神内化为企业高质量发展的强大引擎，团结带领全体党员干部职工，以知难而进、迎难而上的勇气，稳中求进、以进促稳的智慧，致力于将大飞机项目打造成为改革开放的新标杆、创新型国家的新名片，不断开创大飞机事业发展的新篇章，以实际行动为强国建设和民族复兴伟业做出应有的贡献。

This is an article published in the October 2024 issue (No. 19) of the Chinese state-owned enterprise magazine 《国企》(State-Owned Enterprise) on the Commercial Aircraft Corporation of China (COMAC, 中国商飞) official website. The article is authored by the Party Committee of COMAC and discusses how Party-building has guided the company's technological innovation and development of large passenger aircraft in China.

Key content includes:

**Background**: Since the 18th National Congress of the Communist Party of China, the national leadership has prioritized the large aircraft industry. President Xi Jinping visited COMAC's design and research center on May 23, 2014, and met with the C919 project team on September 30, 2022. 2024 marks the 10th anniversary of Xi's inspection of COMAC. "Domestic large aircraft achieving commercial operation" was written into the report of the 20th Party Congress and recognized as a marker of innovation-driven high-quality development.

**Political leadership**: COMAC's Party Committee established mechanisms for implementing Xi Jinping's directives, including a "first agenda item" system for the Party Standing Committee, annual reviews, monthly tracking reports, and the issuance of 18 specific measures in its 2024 Party Committee Document No. 1.

**C919 progress milestones**:
- 2015: C919 completed final assembly (总装下线)
- 2017: First flight (飞上蓝天)
- September 29, 2022: Received type certificate from CAAC after 5+ years of certification, 579 flight test items, and 1,669 tests
- May 28, 2023: First commercial flight from Shanghai Hongqiao to Beijing Capital Airport
- As of September 2024: Safely carried over 500,000 passengers, entering multi-user, multi-fleet operations
- Over 100 major technical challenges were overcome in C919 development over COMAC's 16-year history

**Other aircraft**: The C909 (ARJ21) and C929 (first Chinese long-range wide-body aircraft) have determined their overall technical plans and are in steady development.

**Organization/Party-building innovations**: COMAC established a "functional Party organization + project Party organization" model, setting up temporary Party branches for ARJ21, C919, and C929 project teams. In 2024, the company created 100 Party member demonstration posts, 50 Party member assault teams, and 18 cross-unit joint research teams (including for a scientist's cabin and super-cooled large droplet icing wind tunnel design).

**New ventures**: COMAC incubated two new companies in 2023 — 商飞智能 (COMAC Intelligent, an industrial internet company) and 商飞时代 (COMAC Times, focused on new energy aviation) — both with Party organizations established from their founding.

**Talent development**: COMAC's "Ten Thousand Elite Soldiers Project" (万人精兵工程) builds "4+2" core teams (technical, skills, project, management, plus overseas and urgently-needed talent) and "3+1" scientific innovation main forces. Staff grew from 3,000+ at founding to 17,000+, with over 8,000 technical personnel. The C919 project team was named the first Central Enterprise Outstanding Innovation Team. In January 2024, Chen Yong (COMAC Chief Engineer and ARJ21 Chief Designer) received the "National Outstanding Engineer" award.

**Industry collaboration**: COMAC established 6 large aircraft research institutes with Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Beihang University, Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics, Chongqing University, Tongji University, and Northwestern Polytechnical University, plus an industry-academia-research integration alliance. The company built 1 national engineering research center, 1 national key laboratory, 1 academician workstation, and 9 provincial/municipal-level science and technology innovation platforms. Seven COMAC International Science and Technology Innovation Weeks have been held; the 2024 edition (August 17-23) themed "Green · Intelligent — New Opportunities for Large Aircraft" attracted nearly 500 experts from 59 domestic and international universities and 13 research institutions/enterprises.

**Sustainable aviation fuel (SAF)**: On June 5, 2024, an ARJ21 and C919 completed their first demonstration flights using SAF produced by Sinopec from recycled cooking oil at the Zhenhai Refining plant, advancing green resource utilization.

**Strategic goals**: By 2035, COMAC aims to make the commercial aircraft project a landmark achievement of reform and opening-up, science and technology, and manufacturing strength, becoming a world-class aviation enterprise. By mid-century, it aims to become a world-class aviation enterprise supporting a modern socialist power.

**Culture**: COMAC promotes the "aviation power, four long-terms (long-term struggle, research, hardship, dedication), never give up" entrepreneurial spirit. On September 10, 2024, Air China's first C919 entered commercial service, with a ceremony honoring early aviation pioneers from the "Two Airlines" uprising.

**Footer contact information**: COMAC is headquartered at No. 1919 Expo Avenue, Pudong New District, Shanghai (ZIP 200126), phone +86-21-20888888, with ICP license 沪ICP备12042517号-1.

# 《人民日报》：大飞机，飞出创新发展新高度

时间：2024年11月04日   来源：人民日报

视力保护色：




【字号 [大](javascript:void();) [中](javascript:void();) [小](javascript:void();)】

“我们要做一个强国，就一定要把装备制造业搞上去，把大飞机搞上去，起带动作用、标志性作用。”习近平总书记一直十分关心大飞机事业的发展，曾4次在新年贺词中提及C919大飞机，从“总装下线”“飞上蓝天”，到“正式交付”“实现商飞”，殷殷话语饱含着对国产大飞机的深深期许。

翱翔蓝天的C919，飞出了创新发展的新高度。在大飞机的发展中，我国首次走完了按照国际通行适航标准研制大型客机的全过程，具备了大型客机设计、制造、试验、试飞及适航取证等能力，攻克了一批关键技术、形成了一批核心能力、锤炼了一批人才队伍、带动了一批产业发展。

11月2日，在2024中国航空产业大会暨南昌飞行大会开幕式上，中国商飞C919和ARJ21飞机首次双机编队飞行表演，赢得现场观众热情欢呼。目前，C919已在我国三大航空公司国航、东航、南航投入商业运营，正式迈入多用户多机队运营阶段；与此同时，今年C919首次飞抵拉萨贡嘎国际机场开展高高原运行关键系统研发试飞，首次加注可持续航空燃料执行商业航班任务，首次飞出国门亮相新加坡航展……国产大飞机取得一个又一个新进展。

党的二十届三中全会《决定》提出，“健全新型举国体制，提升国家创新体系整体效能”。让中国大飞机翱翔蓝天，承载着国家意志、民族梦想、人民期盼，满载着新型举国体制下集中力量办大事的磅礴力量。20多个省份，1000余家企业、高校、科研院所，30多万人参与研制，全国上下大力协同，合力攻关，取得了可喜的成就。

目前，C919大型客机累计交付11架，开通9条航线，通航7个城市，安全载客超70万人次。从一颗螺丝钉也要进口，到国产大飞机翱翔蓝天，科学技术从来没有像今天这样推动我国发展进步、造福亿万人民生活。站在新的起点上，我国大飞机规模化和系列化发展正在稳步推进。接续奋斗，我们必将迎来国产大飞机更加美好的前景。

This webpage is from the official website of COMAC (Commercial Aircraft Corporation of China, 中国商用飞机有限责任公司) and features a People's Daily (人民日报) news article dated November 4, 2024, titled "大飞机，飞出创新发展新高度" (Large Aircraft Soaring to New Heights in Innovation and Development).

**Key Points:**

1. **Context**: Chinese President Xi Jinping has mentioned C919 in New Year's addresses four times, tracking its progress from "assembly completion" to "flying," "official delivery," and "commercial operation."

2. **Milestones Achieved**: China completed the full process of developing large passenger aircraft according to international airworthiness standards for the first time, building capabilities in design, manufacturing, testing, flight trials, and airworthiness certification.

3. **Recent Progress (2024)**:
   - On November 2, 2024, COMAC's C919 and ARJ21 aircraft performed their first dual-aircraft formation flight display at the 2024 China Aviation Industry Conference and Nanchang Flight Show.
   - C919 is now in commercial operation with all three major Chinese airlines (Air China, China Eastern, and China Southern), entering multi-user, multi-fleet operations.
   - C919 flew to Lhasa Gonggar Airport for high-altitude plateau key system R&D test flights for the first time.
   - C919 used sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) on a commercial flight for the first time.
   - C919 made its first international appearance at the Singapore Airshow.

4. **Statistics**: 
   - Cumulative delivery: 11 C919 aircraft
   - 9 routes opened
   - Service to 7 cities
   - Over 700,000 passengers safely carried
   - Participation: 20+ provinces, 1,000+ enterprises/universities/research institutes, 300,000+ personnel

5. **Strategic Framework**: The development leverages China's "new type of whole-nation system" (新型举国体制) as emphasized in the 20th CPC Central Committee's Third Plenary Session decisions.

6. **Forward Outlook**: China is steadily advancing toward scaled and serialized development of its large aircraft program.

The article includes photo documentation of C919 operations across airlines, the Lhasa test flight, formation flying at Nanchang, Singapore Airshow performance, and the Farnborough International Airshow exhibition. The page also contains standard footer information including COMAC corporate links, shareholder companies, airline partners, and contact information.

args.summary:
This is the official website of COMAC (Commercial Aircraft Corporation of China, 中国商用飞机有限责任公司), specifically the "Business News" (业务新闻) section. The page lists the company's recent business news items from 2024 to mid-2026, alongside standard website navigation elements.

**Key Aircraft Products:**
- C919 (main narrow-body commercial aircraft)
- C909 (regional aircraft)
- C929 (wide-body aircraft under development)

**Notable News Items (in reverse chronological order):**
- 2026-06: 2026 COMAC Customer Conference held in Guangzhou; 8th "Green COMAC Day" for sustainable aviation
- 2026-03/02: C909 added Alxa Left Banner and Ulanqab routes; 2026 supplier conference; Shanxi Chenggong General Aviation ordered 6 C909 firefighting aircraft; multiple COMAC models displayed at 2026 Singapore Airshow
- 2026-02: C909 medical aircraft conducted overseas free clinic activities in Laos
- 2025-12: C909 aircraft surpassed 30 million cumulative passenger boardings
- 2025-11: C919 and C909 made Middle East debut at Dubai Airshow; "C Family" displayed at 8th China International Import Expo
- 2025-09: 8th COMAC International Science and Technology Innovation Week; C9 Aviation Medical Alliance established; first C909 medical aircraft delivered to China Flying Dragon General Aviation
- 2025-06: COMAC attended 2025 Paris Air Show
- 2025-04/03: C909 began commercial operations in Vietnam; completed first flight in Laos; first C909 delivered to Lao Airlines
- 2024-12: Large aircraft large-scale and serialized construction project launched
- 2024-11: COMAC purchased 4 C919 and 4 C909 full-motion flight simulators; Hong Kong Polytechnic University and COMAC signed agreement to co-build Large Aircraft Research Institute

**Website/Company Information:**
- The company is headquartered at 1919 Shibo Avenue, Pudong New District, Shanghai (postal code 200126)
- Contact: Phone 86-021-20888888, Fax 86-021-68882919
- The website includes links to products, services, human resources, corporate culture, and information disclosure sections

This is a Chinese-language product page from Zivid (a 3D machine vision camera company) focused on robotic welding using 3D vision technology. The page promotes Zivid's 3D color cameras for automated welding applications, highlighting their ability to solve common industrial welding challenges.

Key points covered:
- Zivid 3D vision enables robots to detect, adjust, and precisely weld even when part positioning is imperfect, eliminating the need to constantly reprogram welding paths or fix missed welds.
- The page addresses common challenges in robotic welding and WAAM (Wire Arc Additive Manufacturing): workpiece geometry/location variations causing weld shifting, reflective metal surfaces making sensing unreliable, and heat/spatter/contamination degrading stability.

Three main benefit categories are highlighted:
1. **Stable welding quality** – Avoiding uneven welds, missed points, and costly rework caused by inaccurate depth data and noisy point clouds.
2. **Reliable part handling** – Processing complex geometries, reflective surfaces, and limited camera visibility without compromising precision.
3. **Designed for harsh environments** – Reliable operation in extreme heat, dirt, and welding spatter without frequent recalibration, minimizing downtime.

Key product capabilities include:
- Capturing complete, artifact-free point clouds with millimeter-level accuracy and resolution
- Handling robot-mounted and fixed configurations
- High dynamic range (HDR) imaging for capturing accurate data in both bright and dark areas simultaneously, enabling reliable capture of shiny metals
- Industrial-grade design for extreme heat, vibration, and spatter conditions

The page includes a testimonial quote from Vincent Wegener, Co-founder and General Manager of RAMLAB, praising Zivid cameras: "Zivid cameras met and exceeded our requirements for high-quality 3D sensors. Integration was very simple, and it performs excellently even in very demanding situations like arc welding."

Three real-world application case studies are featured:
1. **RAMLAB MaxQ system** – Robot-mounted 3D vision revolutionizing welding and additive manufacturing.
2. **Pickit** – Multi-robot 3D vision for high-precision car body sealing in automotive production (fixed configuration).
3. **GrayMatter Robotics** – AI-powered robotic surface finishing using Zivid cameras for precise, color-accurate 3D scanning (robot-mounted).

The page contrasts traditional method limitations (failing weld positions on complex geometry, 3D data loss on shiny surfaces, fixed cameras missing optimal angles, expensive/time-consuming camera setup replication) with Zivid's solutions (precise millimeter-level positioning on any geometry, reliable capture of reflective/low-visibility surfaces, flexible mounting for optimized viewing angles, and quickly repeatable deployment of calibrated camera setups across multiple robotic cells).

Call-to-action items include comparing cameras, exploring welding point clouds on Sketchfab, requesting a free demo, and requesting a quote.

焊接间隙变化、元件错位和照明干扰使制造流程中的自动化焊接面临挑战。康耐视视觉解决方案使用先进的 3D 技术和 AI 工具轻松定位元件、引导机械臂并验证焊接质量。这些解决方案在视觉引导的焊接系统中发挥至关重要的作用，以减少手动步骤，提高可追溯性，并使制造商能够可靠处理复杂的焊接任务。

This is a Cognex (康耐视) product/application page describing robot welding automation solutions (机器人焊接自动化). The page highlights the challenges associated with automated welding in manufacturing, including welding gap variations, component misalignment, and lighting interference. Cognex vision solutions use advanced 3D technology and AI tools to locate components, guide robotic arms, and verify welding quality in vision-guided welding systems, reducing manual steps, improving traceability, and enabling manufacturers to handle complex welding tasks reliably.

Key recommended products include:
1. **In-Sight L38 Series** – An AI-driven 3D vision system providing rapid deployment, ease of use, and highly reliable results for advanced inspection, measurement, and guidance applications.
2. **VisionPro Deep Learning software** – AI-driven PC-based image inspection software enabling fast, robust quality control.

The page emphasizes that traditional welding requires manual multi-step processes involving pick-and-place, visual inspection, and accurate seam tracking. Barriers to full automation include spot welding inefficiency, increased reliance on manual intervention, reduced production speed, and quality control impacts. Vision-guided robotics (VGR) overcomes these obstacles by enabling robots to precisely locate, guide, and inspect components on varied assembly lines, freeing operators to focus on higher-level tasks.

Cognex argues that traditional 2D inspection methods fall short of modern high-speed manufacturing demands, missing critical details such as surface defects, misalignment, or subtle changes in weld positioning—especially with complex geometries—leading to quality inconsistency, rework, and safety risks. Cognex's 3D vision systems address these challenges through precise automated inspection and VGR throughout the welding process.

A testimonial quote is featured from Swapnil Talathi, Head of Machine Vision and DPM Control at Wipro PARI: "在未来，我们将管理数千套系统，康耐视肯定会在其中发挥重要作用。" ("In the future, we will manage thousands of systems, and Cognex will certainly play an important role in that.")

The page also offers a downloadable guide titled "对位和机器人引导应用指南" (Guide to Alignment and Robot Guidance Applications) and lists related applications including measurement/dimensional inspection, defect detection and automated inspection, and automated sorting/classification. Cognex headquarters is listed at One Vision Drive, Natick, MA 01760-2059, USA.

<webpage_content>
灯塔工厂再升级！仙工智能助力 3C 电子制造产线智能化流转

项目背景

本期客户是世界500强企业，以其创新的科技理念和领先的技术意识为全球客户提供可编程人机界面、工业平板式计算机、图形逻辑控制器和工业信息终端等产品，在国际工控领域具有良好口碑，是业内主导品牌之一。

客户课题

灯塔工厂是指由世界经济论坛和麦肯锡咨询公司共同选出的数字化制造与全球化4.0的示范者，拥有足够的科技含量与创新性的“世界上最先进的工厂”。 该客户是全球 90 座"灯塔工厂"之一，由于生产车间面积庞大、生产零部件分布零散，各产线的协作以人力+磁条车的形式进行搬运。两边倒工作制再加上难搬运的物料，让企业面临人工成本高、搬运效率低的课题。

解决方案

仙工智能根据该客户存在的各种问题给出一站式智慧物流解决方案，以庞大的产品矩阵分多周期完成整厂的全面升级。目前 1 期方案已投产运行，2 期方案正在实施中，多期后续方案正在有序规划。

### 1 期方案构成：

1. ABM-300J 潜伏顶升式无人搬运底盘  
2. RDS 统一资源调度系统  
3. 梯控模块

### 1 期方案工作流程：

1. 仓库将物料手动拉至仓库缓存位，对应库位检测模块将库位信息传输给 RDS，系统记录库位状态。  
2. 产线员工通过 PDA 向系统下达运输订单  
3. 系统处理后派遣空闲 AMR 将物料运输至接收位置  
4. 完成客户线体装配区与仓库之间的运输

### 实施难点

以往的搬运模式在现场留有大量磁条车，用以搬运产品及杂物。想要对这样的车间进行改造，除去提升效率的课题，如何改快速改造也是巨大挑战。  
综上，客户现场面临以下课题，急需解决：  
1. 磁条车搬运路线长、效率低  
2. 两边倒工作制，劳动强度大  
3. 改造费用高昂，所需周期冗长  
4. 改动程度大将影响生产效率，更大程度上的改造甚至会让工厂停产  
5. 入库、出库、多产线流转，厂内多种物流交接环节复杂 

### 方案亮点：

1. 灵活调度，路线随用随调  
ABM-300J 内部搭载 SRC 系列核心控制器，通过统一资源调度系统 RDS 与工厂系统完美对接，灵活调度。  
2. 直线距离，缩短运输时长  
基于激光 SLAM 的顶升机器人，实现真正的无轨化自主导航，无需改变仓库环境，机器人即可自主穿行，智能拣选与搬运。  
3. 更小盲区，确保人机安全  
搭载前后双激光，双向钻货架更从容；安全触边，保护更到位。  
4. 机器人支持快速充电  
实现 24 小时不间断作业，也极大提升了仓库的安全性  
  
仙工智能与该客户的合作不仅限于此项目，国内多家该客户的工厂均与仙工智能保持密切合作。我们惊喜地发现，客户与现场的工人是更喜欢这些产品的人，他们对于 AMR 的依赖性远超出工程师的想象。  
在产品的长期使用过程中，客户们会不断发掘产品的各种属性，并提出一些新的需求。仙工智能倾听不同的声音，针对性地对产品做出改进，在不断地升级中，帮助客户解决更多实质性的问题，以标准化产品支撑非标方案。

给客户带来的价值

•通过仙工智能一站式智慧物流解决方案，该企业在保证原有生产效率的前提下，以更低的成本、更短的项目周期，实现了工厂的智能升级，经过 1 期改造，车间生产效率得以大幅提升，2 期出入库的改造正在加速进行中！

This case study describes Seer Group's (仙工智能) smart logistics solution upgrade for a lighthouse factory in the 3C electronics manufacturing sector. The client is a Fortune 500 company and one of 90 global "Lighthouse Factories" (as designated by the World Economic Forum and McKinsey), producing programmable human-machine interfaces, industrial panel PCs, graphic logic controllers, and industrial information terminals for the industrial control industry.

**Client Challenges:** The factory's large production area with scattered parts relied on labor plus magnetic strip-guided carts for material transport across production lines. With two-shift work schedules and difficult-to-handle materials, the company faced high labor costs and low transport efficiency. The existing magnetic strip carts had long routes with low efficiency, the retrofit costs were high with lengthy project cycles, and major modifications risked production stoppages. Complex logistics handoffs existed across inbound, outbound, and multiple production lines.

**Solution (Phase 1):** Seer Group deployed a one-stop intelligent logistics solution including:
1. ABM-300J latent lifting AGV chassis (with dual front/rear laser SLAM navigation, safety edge protection, and quick-charge capability for 24-hour operation)
2. RDS (Resource Dispatch System) unified scheduling system integrated with factory systems
3. Elevator control module

**Workflow:** Warehouse workers manually move materials to buffer positions where storage detection modules report status to RDS; production line employees place transport orders via PDA; the system dispatches idle AMRs to transport materials to receiving positions, completing transport between line assembly areas and the warehouse.

**Key Highlights:** Flexible scheduling via RDS, track-free laser SLAM navigation (no warehouse environment changes needed), reduced blind spots for worker safety, and 24/7 uninterrupted operation through fast charging.

**Value Delivered:** The Phase 1 deployment significantly improved production efficiency at lower cost and in a shorter project cycle without sacrificing existing productivity. Phase 2 (inbound/outbound upgrades) is underway with additional phases planned. Seer Group continues close cooperation with multiple factories of this client in China, with ongoing product improvements driven by user feedback to support non-standard solutions with standardized products.

记者实探“智造”工厂：十分钟 “机器人造机器人” ，硬核制造有速度更有温度

2026/08/18 17:32 交汇点新闻

机器人是如何制造出来的？智能制造究竟能为制造业带来怎样的改变？近日，记者走进南京埃斯顿自动化智能工厂，在极具科技感的生产车间找到了答案。

明亮洁净的车间内，无人流水线高速运转，一台台机械臂精准舒展、默契配合，自动完成上料、对位、装配、检测全流程工序，无需人工干预。

![](https://jcdn.xhby.net/dams-res/editing/image/202608/18/abCQlj9dbqZxyvUcxS3ihfUJ.jpg?image_process=resize,w_800/format,jpg) 

令人惊叹的是，从零部件拼装到整机成型，十分钟左右，一台崭新的工业机器人便由机器人自主组装下线。这场“机器造机器”的实景图景，直观诠释了中国智能制造的顶尖精度与极致效率，自主可控的核心技术、持续领跑的市场份额，构筑起中国制造的硬核底气。

这些机器人在现实中有哪些应用场景？“比如，在船舶制造领域，焊接是决定船体品质的核心工序，一艘万吨级船舶的焊缝总长可达数十公里，工作起来是实打实的苦脏累。用机器人便可以替代人工作业。”埃斯顿相关负责人陈欣苇介绍。记者现场了解到，传统船舶焊接作业环境堪称严苛：夏季封闭舱室密不透风，温度超50℃，作业时还有烟尘和弧光，工人必须身着厚重密闭的防护服、防护面罩作业，一轮班次下来浑身湿透、疲惫不堪。艰苦的作业条件，让年轻从业者纷纷望而却步，行业面临人才断层危机。

![](https://jcdn.xhby.net/dams-res/editing/image/202608/18/GpXx2AGytjjRZ2KbxPLnjjcZ.jpg?image_process=resize,w_800/format,jpg) 

机器人的规模化落地，彻底改写了船舶焊接的作业模式。工业机器人可以精准承接重复性、高风险的焊接工序，24小时稳定作业、焊缝均匀饱满。曾经坚守高危一线的工人，得以告别恶劣作业环境，转型投身设备运维、工艺优化、质量管控等技术型、高价值岗位，实现从“体力劳作”到“脑力赋能”的进阶升级。

这份智造温情，同样体现在高温高压的压铸车间。作为汽车零部件、高端五金制造的核心工序，传统压铸车间是制造业公认的艰苦岗位——车间常年高温炙烤，夏季室温超40度。一线工人需全程穿戴厚重防火隔热服，近距离完成高温取件、模具喷涂、毛刺清理等工序，短短几分钟便满身汗湿。

针对压铸行业痛点，搭载高防护、耐高温专用工业机器人便应运而生，无惧高温粉尘、适配恶劣工况，可全自动完成模具喷涂、高温取件等工作，实现无人化闭环生产。智能化改造后，工人彻底远离高温高危机台，劳动强度大幅降低、作业安全全面升级，岗位价值实现质的提升。

AI技术与具身智能的深度融合，为国产机器人产业解锁了全新的发展赛道。依托“AI＋机器人”的创新融合模式，工业机器人不再是只会机械重复作业的设备，而是拥有了自主感知、精准判断、智能思考的能力，真正实现从传统自动化向高阶智能化、智慧化的跨越式升级。埃斯顿公司有关专家介绍，依托行业首创的“机器人站长”协同控制理念，多台机器人可以默契配合、柔性联动、协同作业，仅靠一套控制器就能统筹管控整条工作站的生产流程，大幅提升生产线的柔性程度、生产精度与智能化水平。

![](https://jcdn.xhby.net/dams-res/editing/image/202608/18/zAs0npLTF9kaOf6v4hGmDwrC.jpg?image_process=resize,w_800/format,jpg) 

值得关注的是，从承担生产任务，到与人并肩工作，机器人的角色正在发生转变——协作机器人为我们展示了另一种可能。不同于传统工业机器人作业时需要与人保持安全距离，协作机器人能够进入人与机器共同作业的空间，通过感知环境变化实现减速甚至停止，让这双“手”更加灵活、安全。过去，制造业依靠人的双手；如今，“机械手”正在延伸人的制造能力，从精准执行到柔性协作，不断拓展“智造”的全新可能。

![](https://jcdn.xhby.net/dams-res/editing/image/202608/18/aHcqU3SvGY5BirbN8Vk2mZCX.jpg?image_process=resize,w_800/format,jpg) 

智能制造加速普及，大众常有疑问：全自动化流水线大规模落地，是否会挤压人工岗位？

“智能制造的终极意义，从来不是削减人力，而是赋能人，让劳动者远离危险劳作、奔赴更高质量的岗位。”陈欣苇表示，智能制造从来不是冰冷的技术迭代、简单的“机器换人”，而是以人为本、减负赋能，真正解放人、成就人。

新华日报·交汇点记者 李晞

实习生 杜丽乔

This is a news article from 新华报业网 (Xinhua Daily Media Group) published on August 18, 2026, in which reporter 李晞 (Li Xi) visited the Estun (埃斯顿) Automation smart factory in Nanjing, China, to explore how robots are manufactured and how intelligent manufacturing is transforming industry.

Key highlights:
- In the Estun smart factory's clean, bright production workshop, fully automated assembly lines run 24/7 without human intervention. Robots autonomously complete the entire process including material loading, alignment, assembly, and inspection.
- A new industrial robot can be fully assembled and completed by other robots in approximately 10 minutes, demonstrating "robots making robots" - showcasing China's top precision and efficiency in intelligent manufacturing.

Real-world applications covered in the article:
1. **Shipbuilding/welding**: Traditional ship welding involves extreme conditions - enclosed cabins exceeding 50°C in summer, with smoke, arc light, and heavy protective gear. The industry faces a talent shortage as young workers avoid hazardous jobs. Industrial robots now handle repetitive, high-risk welding tasks 24 hours a day, producing uniform weld seams. Workers transition from physical labor to higher-value technical roles like equipment maintenance, process optimization, and quality control.
2. **Die-casting workshops**: Traditional die-casting plants see summer temperatures exceeding 40°C, requiring workers to wear heavy fireproof gear while handling high-temperature extraction, mold spraying, and burr removal. Specialized high-protection, heat-resistant industrial robots now automate these tasks for unmanned closed-loop production, eliminating workers' exposure to dangerous conditions.
3. **AI and embodied intelligence**: "AI + Robot" integration enables robots to gain autonomous perception, precise judgment, and intelligent thinking capabilities. Estun introduced an industry-first "robot station manager" (机器人站长) collaborative control concept, allowing multiple robots to work flexibly in coordination managed by a single controller across the entire workstation.
4. **Collaborative robots (cobots)**: Unlike traditional industrial robots that require safety distance from humans, collaborative robots can work alongside people, sensing environmental changes to slow down or stop, demonstrating a shift from "precision execution" to "flexible collaboration."

Response to automation concerns: Chen Xinwei (陈欣苇), Estun's relevant official, stated: "智能制造的终极意义，从来不是削减人力，而是赋能人，让劳动者远离危险劳作、奔赴更高质量的岗位" (The ultimate meaning of intelligent manufacturing has never been to cut manpower, but to empower people, allowing workers to move away from dangerous labor toward higher-quality positions). The article emphasizes that intelligent manufacturing is not cold technological iteration or simple "machine replacing man," but people-centered, workload-reducing, and capability-enhancing.

The article was reported by 李晞 and intern 杜丽乔 (Du Liqiao), with editing by 王建朋.
